0 DEC. 1-(AP)-REP. DURHAM (D-NC) SAID TODAY THE 
e Le AND CONFUSED. HE CALLED ON 
“HE ATOMIC ENERGY COMMISSION (AEC) FOR A REAPPRAISAL OF ITS AIMS. 

DURHAM, CHAIRMAN OF THE SENATE-HOUSE ATOMIC ENERGY COMMITTEE, MADE 
1IS VIEWS KNOWN IN A LETTER TO AEC CHAIRMAN LEWIS L. STRAUSS.» 

AMONG OTHER THINGS, DURHAM RENEWED A PROPOSAL OF A 10-YEAR DEMON- 
STRATION POWER REACTOR PROGRAM TO PROVIDE LONG TERM ASSURANCE TO PRIVATE 
INDUSTRY OF GOVERNMENT AID FOR PRIVATE AND PUBLIC ATOMIC POWER 
DEVELOPMENT. 

WRITING STRAUSS, DURHAM ASSERTED: 

*®THERE APPEARS fo BE CONSIDERABLE CONFUSION AS TO WHAT OUR OBJECTIVES 
AND POLICIES ARE, OR SHOULD BE. 

®HOWEVER, THE GENERAL CONSENSUS SEEMS TO BE THAT THE CURRENT ATOMIC 
POWER DEVELOPMENT PROGRAM IS NOT ADEQUATE, PARTICULARLY IF WE TAKE INTO 
ACCOUNT THE OBJECTIVE OF WORLD LEADERSHIP IN REACTOR TECHNOLOGY,® 

DURHAM'’S LETTER APPEARED TO BE ANOTHER INDICATION OF DISSATISFACTION 
AMONG SOME MEMBERS OF CONGRESS OVER DEVELOPMENT OF THE PEACETIME USES 
OF ATOMIC ENERGY, PARTICULARLY IN RELATION TO SOVIET CLAIMS OF ATOMIC 
POWER SUCCESSES. 

THE NORTH CAROLINA DEMOCRAT WROTE STRAUSS THAT DISCUSSIONS AMONG 
SOMMITTEE MEMBERS AND INTERESTED INDIVIDUALS HERE AND ABROAD “HAVE ALL 
POINTED TO THE OVERRIDING NEED FOR A REAPPRAISAL OF OUR POLICIES AND 
MORE PRECISE DEFINITION OF THE POLICY OBJECTIVES IN THE ATOMIC POWER 
DEVELOPMENT PROGRAM, BOTH FROM A DOMESTIC AND INTERNATIONAL STANDPOINT,® 

"ONCE THOSE POLICY OBJECTIVES HAVE BEEN DEFINED," HE ADDED, "THEN IT 
IS BELIEVED NECESSARY TO FORMULATE A REALISTIC AND WELL-BALANCED 
PROGRAM DESIGNED TO CARRY OUT THESE OBJECTIVES ADEQUATELY." 

DURHAM SUGGESTED THAT IN THE NATIONAL INTEREST THE SENATE~HOUSE 
“OMMITTEE AND THE AEC GET TOGETHER INFORMALLY TO TRY AND WORK OUT 
SOME MUTUALLY ACCEPTABLE DEFINITION OF ATOMIC POWER AIMS, AND HOW TO 
PUT THEM IN FORCE. 





IN THIS CONNECTION HE MENTIONED A PROPOSAL FOR A NEW 10-YEAR REACTOR 
OROGRAM HE MADE ORIGINALLY LAST MAY. 

IN SUGCESTING THAT THE COMMITTEE AND AEC JOIN HANDS, DURHAM SAID HE 
HOPED THAT AT LEAST SOME INFORMAL UNDERSTANDINGS COULD BE REACHED ON 
SBIECTIVES AND THE NECESSARY AMOUNT OF GOVERNMENT AID BEFORE CONGRESS 
RETURNS VANCE FOR USE AT 7 PM EST SUNDAY DEC. 1 aN

He snPACRINGTON, DEC a 1 _(AP)=SENA, EASTLAND (D-MISS) SAID TODAY 
TH UN! BLY HIGH STANDARDS OF PROOF® REQUIRED BY THE COMMUNIST 
CONTROL ACT ENABLE MANY COMMUNIST-FRONT ORGANIZATIONS *TO CARRY ON DIS- 
LOYAL ACTIVITIES UNDER A CLOAK OF RESPECTABILITY.® 

EASTLAND, CHAIRMAN OF THE SENATE INTERNAL SECURITY SUBCOMMITTEE 
SAID "THIS APPLIES PARTICULARLY TO RED-CONTROLLED LABOR UNIONS WHICH 
HAVE BEEN EXPELLED BY THE AFL-CIO FOR COMMUNIST DOMINATION.® 

THESE UNIONS CONTINUE TO BE RECOGNIZED BY THE NATIONAL LABOR RELA- 
TIONS BOARD (NLRB) AS BARGAINING AGENTS FOR LARGE NUMBERS OF WORKERS, 
uz SAID, "SIMPLY BECAUSE IT IS IMPOSSIBLE UNDER PRESENT STANDARDS OF 
PROOF TQ LEGALLY DESIGNATE THEM AS SUBVERSIVE-LED ORGANIZATIONS." 

AS "A CASE IN POINT" EASTLAND CITED THE AMERICAN COMMUNICATIONS ASSN. 
(ACA), AN INDEPENDENT UNION REPRESENTING SOME 8,000 EMPLOYES OF WESTERN 
UNION AND RCA AND OTHER COMMUNICATIONS FIRMS IN THE NEW YORK METROPOLI- 
TAN AREAe 

EASTLAND'S STATEMENT WAS MADE IN ANNOUNCING PUBLICATION BY THE SUB- 
COMMITTEE OF TESTIMONY TAKEN AT PUBLIC HEARINGS LAST MAY FROM JOSEPH P. 
SELLY. PRESIDENT OF THE COMMUNICATIONS UNION, AND OTHERS. 

“We HAVE SWORN TESTIMONY THAT THE OFFICERS OF THIS UNION HAVE BEEN 
MEMBERS, AT LEAST IN THE PAST, OF THE COMMUNIST PARTY," EASTLAND SAID. 

"AND WHEN A NUMBER OF ACA OFFICERS APPEARED BEFORE’ THE SUBCOMMITTEE 
RECENTLY, THEY ALL INVOKED THE FIFTH AMENDMENT IN REFUSING TO SAY 
WHETHER OR NOT THEY WERE MEMBERS," HE ADDED. 

SELLY WAS AMONG THOSE WHO REFUSED TO ANSWER WHEN ASKED ABOUT COMMU - 
NIST MEMBERSHIP. 

THE COMMUNIST CONTROL ACT, PASSED BY CONGRESS IN 1954, PROVIDES 
FOR DENYING ANY LABOR ORGANIZATION FOUND TO BE COMMUNISTINFILTRATED OR 
COMMUNIST-DOMINATED THE RIGHT TO SERVE AS A COLLECTIVE BARGAINING AGENT 
UNDER THE TAFT-HARTLEY LABOR RELATIONS ACT. 

AMONG THE REQUIRED STANDARDS OF PROOF IS A SHOWING THAT SUCH ORGANIZA 
TIONS ARE RUN BY ONE OR MORE PERSONS WHO ARE, OR WITHIN TWO YEARS HAVE 
BEEN, COMMUNIST PARTY MEMBERS OR COMMUNIST ACENTS. 


IN THE HEARINGS ON THE ACA, REFERENCE WAS MADE TO THE DIFFICULTY OF 
ESTABLISHING PROOF OF COMMUNIST PARTY MEMBERSHIP. 

EASTLAND SAID THAT ALTHOUGH THE GREAT MAJORITY OF THE ACA MEMBERS ARE 
LOYAL ANERICANS, "THEY MUST DEPEND ON COMMUNIST LEADERSHIP TO BARGAIN 

"EFFORTS TO OUST THE LEADERSHIP HAVE BEEN FOILED BECAUSE THESE coM- 
MUNIST OFFICERS CONTROL THE MACHINERY OF UNION ELECTIONS,® HE SAID.

DECe 1 (AP)-MORE AND MORE AMERICANS WILL HAVE TO TAKE ON DUAL 
= =--IF THE COUNTRY SUPPLIES THE

MAINE REPUBLICAN, SAID TONIGHT. 

SEN. SMITH, A LIEUTENANT COLONEL IN THE WAF RESERVE, ARRIVED AT 
STRATEGIC AIR’ COMMAND HEADQUARTERS WHERE SHE WILL INTERVIEW OFFICERS 
AND NEN FOR THE NEXT FEW DAYS AT THE REQUEST OF THE SECRETARY OF THE 
AIR . 

®MY CURRENT DUTY IS CENTERED ON TRYING TO FIND OUT WHY SO MANY 
MISSILE TECHNICIANS ARE LEAVING THE AIR FORCE AND WHAT CAN BE DONE TO 
MAKE THE SERVICE SUFFICIENTLY ATTRACTIVE TO KEEP THEM IN," SHE SAID. 

ADDRESSING THE RESERVE OFFICERS ASSN. TONIGHT, THE SENATOR ENLARGED 
ON THAT THEME, EXPLAINING THAT THE ARMED FORCES GANNOT COMPETE WITH 
PRIVATE INDUSTRY IN A WAGE OR PAY WAR. 

®I THINK THAT PRIVATE INDUSTRY WILL WIN CONSTANTLY IN SUCH A 
COMPETITIVE STRUGCLE BECAUSE PRIVATE INDUSTRY WILL ALWAYS BE ABLE TO 
PAY MORE," SHE SAID. ADDING THAT THE END RESULT WOULD BE A CONSTANT 
SPIRALING OF WAGES AND NATIONAL DEFENSE COSTS. 

THE ANSWER, SHE CONTINUED, LIES INTHE DUAL STATUS SYSTEM. 

"IT SEEMS TO ME THAT INEVITABLY THE SOLUTION MUST BE THAT SUCH 
TECHNICIANS ARE GOING TO TAKE ON HALF-AND-HALF ROLES, IN WHICH THEY 
THEIR WORK MUST BE INTE- 
GRATED BETWEEN THE FIRM THEY ARE EMPLOYED BY AND THE SERVICE.® 

THE SYSTEM, SHE BELIEVES, WOULD MAKE FOR UTILIZATION OF MANPOWER 
FOR NATIONAL DEFENSE AT LES2 COST TO THE TAXPAYERS, AND "IT WILL CIVE 
THE TECHNICIANS THOSE THINGS WHICH ATTRACT THEM FROM THE ARMED 
SERVICES TO PRIVATE INDUSTRY WITHOUT THE ARMED SERVICES LOSING THEM."

OF BEING A WESTERN PUPPET, A TRAITOR TO ARAB NATIONALISM AND OF BEING 
IN SECRET NEGOTIATIONS TO’SELL OUT TO ISRAEL. THEY EVEN HINTED HE 
OUGHT TO BE ASSASSINATED. HUSSEIN, IN TURN, ACCUSED EGYPT'S LEADERS 
OF BEING TOOLS OF COMMUNISM AND OF TRYING TO STIR UP MUTINY IN HIS ARMY. 

TODAY EGYPTIAN CHARGE D'AFFAIRES SAID GHAMRAWEY PAID A SURPRISE 
CALL ON SAMIR RIFAI, JORDAN'S DEPUTY PREMIER AND FOREICN MINISTER. 

HE INFORMED RIFAI OF EGYPT'S "FULL SUPPORT® IN JORDAN'S BLOCKADE OF MT. 
SCOPUS AND BOYCOTT OF U.S. MARINE COL.sBYRON LEARY, ACTING CHIEF OF THE 
U.N. TRUCE SUPERVISION ORCANIZATION. 

HAMMARSKJOLD, SINCE ARRIVING HERE YESTERDAY, HAS HAD 10 HOURS OF 
TALKS WITH HUSSEIN, RIFAI, PREMIER IBRAHIM HASHEM AND OTHER OFFICIALS 
IN AN EFFORT TO GET AN AGREEMENT ABOUT ISRAELI CONVOYS TO MT.SCOPUS. 

SOME QUARTERS IN AMMAN GLOOMILY PREDICTED ANYTHING COULD HAPPEN IF 
THERE IS NO SETTLEMENT BY WEDNESDAY, WHEN ISRAEL'S NEXT CONVOY IS 
SCHEDULED TO GO THROUGH. THE IDEA BEING CONVEYED WAS THAT ISRAEL MIGHT 
TRY TO SHOOT HER WAY THROUGH. 

HAMMARSKJOLD'S AIDES ADMITTED THE SITUATION WAS URGENT AND COULD 
BECOME EXTREMELY SERIOUS UNLESS SETTLED QUICKLY, BUT EXPRESSED DOUBT 
IT WOULD LEAD TO ANY SHOOTING WEDNESDAY. FOR ONE THING, THEY SAID 
HAMMARSKJOLD WOULD BE IN ISRAEL THAT DAY, AND THEY DOUBTED ISRAEL WOULD 


TRY TO PUSH A CONVOY THROUGH BY MILITARY PRESSURE WHILE NEGOTIATIONS 
WERE STILL GOING ON. 

MT»SCOPUS IS A LOW HILL ONLY 900 FEET LONG AND 400 FEET WIDE ENCLOSED 
BY JORDAN-HELD TERRITORY JUST OUTSIDE THE OLD WALLED CITY OF JERUSALEM. 
ISRAEL WAS LEFT IN POSSESSION OF THE BIT OF TERRITORY BY THE 1949 
ARMISTICE. THE JEWISH HADASSAH HOSPITAL, HEBREW UNIVERSITY AND A LIBRA® 
ARE LOCATED THERE BUT HAVE NOT BEEN OPERATED SINCE THE ARMISTICE. 

ONCE EVERY TWO WEEKS FOR YEARS THE ISRAELIS HAVE SENT A SUPPLY CONVOY 
ABOUT A MILE THROUGH JORDAN TERRITORY TO THE CARETAKER FORCE AT MT. 
SCOPUS. IT USUALLY CONSISTED OF FOUR TO EIGHT VEHICLES DRIVEN BY U.N. 
PERSONNEL. AFTER LEAVING ISRAEL THROUGH THE FAMOUS MADELBAUM GATE IN 
JERUSALEM IT WAS ESCORTED BY JORDAN SOLDIERS TO THE FOOT OF THE HILL.

THE OCT. 3 SHOOTING. THE SOLDIER WAS GUARDING LOADED FREIGHT CARS

THE SENTENCE IN VIEW OF BAILEY’S PAST ARMY RECORD AND WHAT SHE TERMED 
THE "PATENTLY UNINTENTIONAL” CHARACTER OF THE OFFENSE. 
THE 8TH ARMY SAID BAILEY WOULD BE ELIGIBLE TO RETURN TO DUTY AT THE 
END OF FOUR MONTHS. THE DECISION WHETHER TO ERASE THE BAD CONDUCT 
DISCHARGE WILL DEPEND UPON HIS CONDUCT IN PRISON AT FT. ORD, CALIF.,

: DEC. 3 (AP)-THE UNITED STATES THREW ITS 
oleh n:dtv oboe deboh wana Sine FE ON HOW TO END THE THREE- 
YEAR-OLD REBELLION IN ALGERIA 
UeSe AMBASSADOR HENRY CABOT LODGE TOLD THE S2-NATION UeNe 
POLITICAL COMMITTEE THAT THE UNITED STATES BELIEVES FRANCE SHOULD HAVE 
"FURTHER OPPORTUNITY TO FOSTER POLITICAL EVOLUTION TOWARD THE COMMON 
OBJECTIVE OF STABILITY AND PEACE IN ALGERIA." ; 
HE SAID THIS SHOULD BE DONE IN A WAY ®WHICH WILL SATISFY THE 
ASPIRATIONS OF ALL THE PEOPLE OF ALGERIA.® 
LODGE SPOKE AFTER SOVIET DELEGATE ARKADY As SOBOLEV IN A GENERALLY 
MILD SPEECH CALLED FOR A SOLUTION OF THE ALGERIAN PROBLEM IN A MANNER 
THAT WOULD BE BOTH IN THE INTERESTS OF THE ALGERIANS AND THE FRENCH. 
BUT SOBOLEV MADE CLEAR THE SOVIET UNION SUPPORTED THE CLAIM OF ALGERIAN 
NATIONALISTS TO INDEPENDENCE, AND THAT IT REGARDED THE FRENCH MEASURES 
IN NORTH AFRICA AS "MILITARY COLONIALISM." 
NOW THAT THE UNITED STATES HAS TAKEN THE WRAPS OFF ITS POSITION, 
THE ARAB-ASIAN NATIONS ARE EXPECTED TO SUBMIT A RESOLUTION CALLING ON 
FRANCE TO RECOGNIZE THE RIGHT OF ALGERIANS TO DETERMINE THEIR OWN 
POLITICAL FREEDOM, AND TO NEGOTIATE WITH THEM. BUT WITH U.S. SUPPORT 
LACKING, CHANCES FOR U.N. APPROVAL APPEAR DIMe 
THE UNITED STATES WAS IN A TICKLISH POSITION. THE ARAB NATIONS 
SOUGHT UsSe SUPPORT OF THE OFFER BY TUNISIA AND MOROCCO TO MEDIATE THE 
ALGERIAN DISPUTE. FRANCE. AN ALLY OF THE UNITED STATES IN THE NORTH 
ATLANTIC TREATY ORGANIZATION, HAS TURNED THE OFFER DOWN. 


LODGE TOLD THE COMMITTEE THE UNITED STATES APPRECIATES "THE 
WORTHY MOTIVES UNDERLYING THIS OFFER AND THE CONCILIATORY AND 
ONSTRUCTIVE SPIRIT IN WHICH IT BEEN MADE. 3 
ONBUT HE ADDED THAT IN ORDER TO MAKE ANY PROGRESS THE OFFER REQUIRES 
THE SUPPORT OF FRANCE. 

sir FRANCE DOES NOT FEEL THAT UNDER EXISTING CIRCUMSTANCES THE 
OFFER OF GOOD OFFICES CAN BRING ABOUT A SATISFACTORY SOLUTION AT THIS 
TIME, IT IS HOPED THAT CIRCUMSTANCES IN THE NOT TOO DISTANT FUTURE 
WILL’MAKE IT POSSIBLE FOR STEPS SUCH AS THESE OR OTHERS TO BE TAKEN 
WHICH WOULD PROMOTE A PEACEFUL SOLUTION," LODGE SAID. 

HE SAID FRANCE TOOK A ®STEP FORWARD" LAST WEEK WITH ADOPTION OF A 
LEGISLATIVE PROGRAM AIMED AT GIVING ALGERIANS A NEW POLITICAL SETUP 
WITHIN THE FRENCH UNION. 

HE ASSERTED THE UNITED STATES WELCOMED THE REITERATION OF FOREIGN 
MINISTER CHRISTIAN PINEAU THAT FRANCE INTENDED TO SEEK A CEASE-FIRE, 
HOLD GENERAL ELECTIONS "AND WORK OUT WITH THE ELECTED REPRESENTATIVES 
A NEW STRUCTURE FOR ALGERIA.® 

_ ARAB_AND ASIAN NATIONS HAVE REJECTED THE FRENCH PLAN, SAYING A 
CEASE-FIRE CAN COME ONLY AFTER FRANCE AGREES TO NEGOTIATE. 

SOVIET DELEGATE SOBOLEV CHARGED THAT OIL EXPLORATION IN THE SAHARA 
HAS BEEN PLAYING AN INCREASINGLY LARGER ROLE IN FRENCH POLICY, AND THAT 
THE INTERESTS OF AMERICAN "OIL MONOPOLISTS" ARE INVOLVED. 

(SOBOLEV SAID THE AMERICANS ARE TRYING TO PUSH THE FRENCH OUT OF THE 
EXPLORATION PICTURE, AND ALLEGED THIS WAS A MOVE COINCIDING WITH U.S. 
MILITARY INTERESTS IN NORTH AFRICA. 


"THERE IS A SMACK OF OIL WHICH MIXES IN WITH THE SMELL OF BLOOD FROM 
ALGERIA COMING FROM THE SAHARA,® HE DECLARED.

THE RULER OF NINE MILLION ARABS ADDRESSED A DINNER OF THE WORLD 
AFFAIRS COUNCIL OF NORTHERN CALIFORNIA AFTER RECEIVING A 21-GUN 
ARRIVAL SALUTE AT INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT AND MAKING AN UNSCHEDULED 
INCOGNITO VISIT TO THE AUTO SHOW AT THE COW PALACE. 

"THE MAINTENANCE OF PEACE, THE CONSOLIDATION OF INTERNATIONAL 
RELATIONS, THE SUBSTITUTION OF COLLABORATION AND SOLIDARITY FOR ANTA- 
GONISM AND DISTRUST BETWEEN PEOPLES--THESE CONSTITUTE THE FUNDAMENTAL 
PRINCIPLES OF ISLAM," SAID KING MOHAMMED. HIS TALK WAS TRANSLATED. 

"OUR RECNT HISTORY HAS SERVED ONLY TO STRENGTHEN OUR BELIEFS 
IN THESE PRINCIPLES.® 

THE KING DID NOT MENTION ARMED CONFLICT IN PROGRESS BETWEEN IFNIAN 
TRIBESMEN AND SPANISH TROOPS IN THE SMALL AREA OF IFNI STILL CLAIMED 
AS A COLONY OF SPAIN. 

SPAIN SURRENDERED PROTECTORATE RIGHTS IN APRIL 1956 OVER THE 
NORTH OF MORROCO THE REALM NOW RULED BY KING MOHAMMED AND THE SITE 
OF MAJOR Ue Se AiR FORCE BASES IN NORTH AFRICA. 

A SPOKESMAN SAID MOROCCO WOULD APPEAL TO THE UNITED NATIONS IF 
SPANISH FORCES FIGHTING THE IFNIAN REBELS CONTINUED AGGRESSION INTO 
MOROCCAN TERRITORY. 

SOON AFTER ARRIVING BY PLANE FROM LOS ANGELES, KING MOHAMMED 
MADE A SURPRISE APPEARANCE BEFORE A CONVENTION oF UNITED STATES MAYORS 
AND CITY OFFICIALS. 


SPEAKING IN HIS NATIVE TONGUE TO MORE THAN 1,500 PERSONS ATTENDING 
THE AMERICAN MUNICIPAL ASSNe, KING MOHAMMED SAID HIS PEOPLE WERE ABOUT 
TO ENTER INTO THEIR FIRST MUNICIPAL ELECTIONS. 

"MY PEOPLE HOPE TO PROFIT BY YOUR EXPERIENCES AND TO ESTABLISH A 
HAPPY CONDITION OF DEMOCRACY IN MY COUNTRY,” THE NORTH AFRICAN RULER 
ASSERTED IN A SPEECH LATER TRANSLATED INTO ENGLISH.

EASTLAND'S COMMENTS WERE MADE IN A STATEMENT ANNOUNCING THE SUB- 
COMMITTEE'S PUBLICATION OF TESTIMONY IT RECEIVED AT A PUBLIC HEARING 
LAST AUGUST ABOUT FIELD'S ACTIVITIES AS A CHURCH RELIEF WORKER IN EUROPE 
DURING AND SHORTLY AFTER WORLD WAR Ile 

FIELD HAS BEEN NAMED IN EARLIER CONGRESSIONAL INQUIRIES AS A MEMBER 
OF THE COMMUNIST UNDERGROUND HERE IN THE EARLY 1930S, WHILE HE WAS 
WORKING FOR THE STATE DEPARTMENT.« 

IN 1949 HE WAS ARRESTED BEHIND THE IRON CURTAIN AS A SPY FOR THE 
UNITED STATES, BUT IN 1954 THE HUNGARIAN GOVERNMENT ANNOUNCED HE HAD 
BEEN CLEARED AND HE WAS RELEASED FROM PRISON. 

FIELD CHOSE TO REMAIN IN HUNGARY, AND THE SUBCOMMITTEE SAID THAT AT 
LAST REPORT HE WAS WORKING AS A TRANSLATOR IN A GOVERNMENT PRINTING 

FROM 1941 UNTIL HIS DISMISSAL IN 1947 HE DIRECTED RELIEF WORK IN 
i FRANCE AND ELSEWHERE IN EUROPE FOR THE UNITARIAN SERVICE COMMITTEE. 

FRANK KETCHAM, WASHINGTON COUNSEL FOR THE CHURCH ORGANIZATION, TES- 
TIFIED LAST AUGUST THAT IT BEGAN TO RECEIVE REPORTS IN 1946 THAT FIELD 
WAS A COMMUNIST AND WAS PARTIAL TO COMMUNISTS IN HIS RELIEF WORK. 

KETCHAM SAID FIELD DENIED THIS AND THAT THE CHURCH ORGANIZATION WAS 
UNABLE TO FIND SUBSTANTIATING EVIDENCE BUT NONETHELESS DECIDED *HE HAD 
TO GO" AND DROPPED HIM IN 1947 FOR "BUDGETARY REASONS.” 

EASTLAND SAID THE EVIDENCE SHOWED THAT "FIELD SURREPTITIOUSLY DI- 
VERTED THE HUMANITARIAN RESOURCES OF A CHURCH ORGANIZATION TO FURTHER 
THE UNGODLY AIMS OF INTERNATIONAL COMMUNISM." 

"BY HIS STEALTHY ACTS." EASTLAND ADDED, "HE DECEIVED THE EMPLOYER 
TO WHOM HE OWED HIS PROFESSIONAL LOYALTY AND WAS GUILTY OF TREASONABLE 
ACTS AGAINST THE COUNTRY OF WHICH HE WAS A CITIZEN.®

ARRANGED." SHE IS THE MOTHER OF JOHN Te DOWNEY, 27, WHO WAS CAPTURED 
WITH FECTEAU.

OBJECTIONS. SO FAR NO AMERICAN REPORTERS HAVE GONE IN.

)-ITALY TODAY PROPOSED THAT THE UNITED STATES 
N CREATING A SPECIAL FUND TO DEVELOP MIDDLE 


, “EAST AND MEDITERRANEAN COUNTRIES. 


FOREIGN MINISTER GIUSEPPE PELLA MADE THE PROPOSAL TO SECRETARY OF 


«STATE DULLES AT A MEETING ON NEW MOVES TO COPE WITH RUSSIA'S STEPPED-UP 


SHALLENGE TO THE FREE WORLD. 

PELLA SUGGESTED THE UNITED STATES CONTRIBUTE TO THIS FUND ALL MONEY 
[HAT EUROPEAN COUNTRIES ARE DUE TO REPAY IN THE NEXT FEW YEARS ON U.S. 
MARSHALL PLAN ASSISTANCE LOANS. 

THE EUROPEAN COUNTRIES WOULD CONTRIBUTE AN AMOUNT EQUAL TO 20 PER 
SENT OF SUCH REPAYMENTS AS THEIR SHARE IN THE PLAN. 

EUROPEAN COUNTRIES WHICH HAVE NO SUCH MARSHALL PLAN REPAYMENTS 
JOULD CONTRIBUTE TO THE FUND INDEPENDENTLY. NO PAYMENT BY THEM WOULD 
EXCEED THE MAXIMUM PAID BY MARSHALL PLAN NATIONS. 

PELLA PROPOSED THE NEW MIDEAST FUND, INFORMANTS SAID, BECAUSE HE 
FIRMLY BELIEVES A NEW JOINT WESTERN INITIATIVE IS NEEDED IN THE AREA TO 
SOLVE URGENT PROBLEMS. 

THE PROPOSED FUND WOULD BE DIRECTED BY A NINE-MEMBER MANAGING BOARD 
OF WHICH AN AMERICAN REPRESENTATIVE WOULD BE CHAIRMAN. 

PELLA PROPOSED THAT THE NATIONS SETTING UP THE FUND BE THE MEMBERS 
OF THE ORGANIZATION OF EUROPEAN ECONOMIC COOPERATION (OEEC). THESE 
NATIONS, WHO BANDED TOGETHER IN 1948 TO HELP DRAW UP THE MARSHALL PLAN, 
ARE: BRITAIN, FRANCE, WEST GERMANY, ITALY, BELGIUM, THE NETHERLANDS 
LUXEMBOURG, DENMARK, ICELAND, NORWAY, PORTUGAL, GREECE, TURKEY, IRELAND, 
SWEDEN, SWITZERLAND AND AUSTRIA. IN’ ADDITION CANADA AND SPAIN ARE 
ASSOCIATE MEMBERS.

THE PUBLIC, THE FEDERAL COMMUNICATIONS SAID ee 


ALL TELEVISION AND RADIO STATIONS WILL BE PERMITTED TO USE CONELRAD 
"ATTENTION SIGNALS" TO INTERRUPT REGULAR PROGRAMMING FOR EMERGENCY 
WEATHER BUREAU WARNINGS OF HURRICANES, TORNADOES, FLOODS AND OTHER 
DANGEROUS WEATHER CONDITIONS, THE FCC’ ANNOUNCED. 

THESE "ATTENTION SIGNALS,* CONSISTING OF TWO TIMED BREAKS IN THE 
BROADCASTING SIGNAL, FOLLOWED BY A DISTINCTIVE SHARP TONE, AUTO- 
MATICALLY -WILL TURMON THOUSANDS-OF-CONELRAD ALERT RECEIVERS WHICH 
HAVE BEEN INSTALLED IN SCHOOLS, INDUSTRIAL PLANTS, POLICE STATIONS, 
CIVIL DEFENSE AGENCIES AND MANY HOMES. 

THE FCC NOTED THAT USE OF THE SYSTEM WILL NOT ONLY PROVIDE QUICK 
WARNING, BUT ALSO WILL ELIMINATE MUCH OF THE TELEPHONE LINE JAMMING, 
WHICH ALMOST ALWAYS OCCURS IN SEVERE WEATHER. 

THE IDEA OF PUTTING CONELRAD, A WARTIME DEFENSE DEVICE, INTO THIS 
SECONDARY PEACETIME FUNCTION, FCC SAID, WAS DISCUSSED INFORMALLY 
LAST APRIL AT A CONFERENCE OF THE NATIONAL ASSN. OF RADIO AND TELEVISION 
BROADCASTERS IN CHICAGO. 

IN JUNE OF THIS YEAR, THE PLAN WAS PROPOSED FORMALLY TO THE FCC 
BY LARRY BURROWS, CHIEF ENGINEER OF RADIO STATION KMOX, ST. LOUIS, MO. 

CONELRAD IS THE SHORT NAME FOR "CONTROL OF ELECTROMAGNETIC 
RADIATION." WHEN ENEMY ATTACK BY BOMBERS OR GUIDED MISSILES IS 
EXPECTED, THE SIGNAL FOR THE ALERT IS TRANSMITTED TO BROADCASTING 
STATIONS BY THE UsSe AIR FORCE. THEN, MANY STATIONS WOULD LEAVE THE 
AIR ENTIRELY, WHILE REMAINING KEY STATIONS SHIFT TO 640 OR 1240 
KILOCYCLES FOR BROADCASTING, THUS DEPRIVING THE ENEMY OF A RADIO 
NAVIGATIONAL AID. 

IN THE "EMERGENCY WEATHER WARNING SYSTEM" THE STATIONS WOULD GET 
THEIR ALERT FROM THE WEATHER BUREAU AND WOULD REMAIN ON THEIR REGULAR 


FREQUENCIES WHILE BROADCASTING T AT TINS.

-—plitirteaMRAtONs, NaYag DEC. 6 CAP )=THE UNITED STATES TOLD THE 

UeNe TODAY THAT ANY MORE EFFORTS TO REACH AGREEMENT ON A DRAFT CONVEN- 
TION ON FREEDOM OF INFORMATION IS "A WASTE OF UNITED NATIONS TIME AND 


RESOURCES." 
PHILIP KLUTZNICK OF CHICAGO, A MEMBER OF THE UsS. DELEGATION, OUT- 
LINED THE UeS. VIEW IN A SPEECK BEFORE THE U.N. SOCIAL COMMITTEE. 
EFFORTS TO REACH AGREEMENT ON SUCH A CONVENTION HAVE BEEN MADE 
IN THE U.N. SINCE 1951, THE WESTERN NATIONS TAKE THE VIEW THAT A 
MINIMUM OF RESTRICTIONS SHOULD BE APPLIED TO FREEDOM OF INFORMATION. 
OTHER NATIONS, MAINLY THE MIDDLE EASTERN, LATIN AMERICAN AND ASIAN 
COUNTRIES, WANT RESTRICTIONS THEY SAY WILL PROTECT THEM FROM WHAT THEY 
MIGHT CONSIDER UNFAIR AND IRRESPONSIBLE REPORTING} 
"THE UNITED STATES IS OPPOSED TO THE DRAFT CONVENTION ON FREEDOM 
OF INFORMATION," KLUTZNICK SAID. "WE OPPOSE THIS CONVENTION BECAUSE 
IT HAS BECOME IN EFFECT A PROPOSAL TO LIMIT AND RESTRICT THE BASIC 
HUMAN RIGHTS OF FREEDOM OF SPEECH AND OF THE PRESS~ 
"AS SUCH, IT IS IN DIRECT CONTRADICTION To THE PRINCIPLES 
AND OBJECTIVES OF THE UeNe AND UsNe EDUCATIONAL, SCIENTIFIC AND CULTURAL 
ORGANIZATION AND SHOULD BE REJECTED BY THIS BODY."

THE YUGOSLAV INFORMANTS SAID YUGOSLAVIA WANTS TO CONTINUE FRIENDLY 
ECONOMIC AND POLITICAL RELATIONSHIPS WITH THE UNITED STATES. 

AMERICAN MILITARY AID WAS FIRST GRANTED TO YUGOSLAVIA AFTER IT 
WAS BOOTED OUT OF THE SOVIET-LED COMINFORM IN 1948. BILLIONS OF 
DOLLARS IN MILITARY AID HAVE BEEN GRANTED TO YUGOSLAVIA SINCE. 

AFTER YUGOSLAVIA AND THE SOVIET UNION GRADUALLY BEGAN DRAWING 
CLOSER TOGETHER, THE UNITED STATES BEGAN RECONSIDERING ITS AID 
POLICY. LAST OCTOBER AFTER A BREAK OF SEVERAL MONTHS, PRESIDENT 
EISENHOWER DECIDED THE AID SHOULD BE CONTINUED. AT PRES 
MILITARY AID IS AGAIN BEING REAPPRAISED.

APPROVED YUGOSLAV REFUSAL TO SIGN THE MAIN DECLARATION WHICH EMERGED 
FROM THE MOSCOW TALKS OF RULING COMMUNIST PARTIES DURING THE CELE- 
BRATIONS OF THE 40TH ANNIVERSARY OF THE BOLSHEVIK REVOLUTION. 

THE OFFICIAL NEWS AGENCY, TANJUG, SAID A PLENARY SESSION OF THE 
CENTRAL COMMITTEE MET TODAY AT BRIONI, WHERE VICE PRESIDENT EDVARD 
KARDELJ SUBMITTED A REPORT ON ACTIVITIES OF THE YUGOSLAV COMMUNIST 
PARTY DELEGATION IN MOSCOW. 

THE CENTRAL COMMITTEE "APPROVED THE WORK AND REPORT OF THE DELEGA- 
TION," THE COMMUNIQUE SAID, ADDING THAT THE COMMITTEE CONSIDERED THE 
DELEGATION ACTED CORRECTLY WHEN IT DID NOT PARTICIPATE AT THE 
MEETING OF 12 COMMUNIST PARTIES AND DID NOT SIGN THE RESULTING 
DECLARATION. DISCLOSURE THAT THE YUGOSLAVS DID NOT PARTICIPATE IN 
THE MEETING INDICATES THEY KNEW WHAT THE DECLARATION WOULD CONTAIN. 

@ THE DECLARATION "CONTAINED CERTAIN ATTITUDES AND APPRAISALS WHICH 
ARE CONTRARY WITH THE ATTITUDE OF THE UNION OF COMMUNISTS OF 
YUGOSLAVIA AND WHICH IT CONSIDERS AS INCORRECT,® THE COMMUNIQUE SAID. 

BUT THE CENTRAL COMMITTEE BELIEVES THAT IN SPITE OF "DIFFERENCES IN 
OUTLOOK ON DEFINITE PROBLEMS WHICH EXIST BETWEEN THE UNION OF 
COMMUNISTS OF YUGOSLAVIA AND CERTAIN OTHER COMMUNIST PARTIES THIS 
INEED NOT AND SHOULD NOT BE A HINDERANCE FOR DEVELOPMENT OF 
FRATERNAL COOPERATION.® 

THIS IS THE FIRST TIME SINCE THE MEETING BETWEEN TITO AND NI 
KHRUSHCHEV IN AUGUST IN ROMANIA THAT ®DIFFERENCES IN OPINION" 49° 4° 
BETWEEN YUGOSLAV AND SOVIET COMMUNISTS HAVE COME TO PUBLIC NOTICE “¥¢ 

WHILE THE COMMUNIQUE DID NOT SPECIFY THE DIFFERENCES, THE 
UNDERSTANDING HERE IS THAT YUGOSLAVIA DID NOT SIGN THE MOSCOW 
DECLARATION BECAUSE IT STRESSED THE LEADING ROLE OF THE SOVIET 
COMMUNIST PARTY, CALLED FOR STRENGTHENING OF THE WARSAW MILITARY 
PACT AND VIOLENTLY ASSAILED WESTERN COUNTRIES~ 

YUGOSLAV COMMUNISTS WERE SAID TO HAVE FELT THAT BY SIGNING THE 
DECLARATION, YUGOSLAVIA WOULD ABANDON HER OPPOSITION TO POWER BLOCS. 


_ JITO"S REMARKS TO THE CENTRAL COMMITTEE MEETING WERE BROADCAST TO- 
NIGHT BY RADIO BELGRADE. TITO REBUKED THOSE WHO APPLY THE NAME 
REVISIONIST TO YUGOSLAV COMMUNISTS. 

HE MENTIONED NO NAMES, BUT HIS REBUKE WAS BELIEVED AIMED AT THE 
SOVIET UNION'S COMMUNIST PARTY AND AT THE SOVIET-LED COMMUNIST BLOC. 

A REVISIONIST IS COMMUNIST JARGON FOR SOMEONE WHO DEVIATES FROM 
ACCEPTED PARTY POLICY. 

TITO TOLD THE CENTRAL COMMITTEE YUGOSLAV COMMUNISTS HAVE BEEN CALLED 
REVISIONISTS SINCE THE 1948 BREAK WITH MOSCOW AND THAT SIMILAR CHARGES 
ARE STILL BEING MADE. 

"WE MUST," TITO SAID, "CONTINUE TO REJECT SUCH CHARGES. WE DO NOT 
PRETEND TO BE ANYTHING ELSE THAN EQUAL AMONG EQUALS." 

TITO"S STATEMENT WAS BELIEVED PROMPTED BY THE FACT THAT SOME COMMU- 
NISTS HAVE BEEN CALLING THE YUGOSLAV COMMUNISTS REVISIONISTS BECAUSE 
THEY DID NOT SIGN THE MOSCOW DELCARATIONs | orc

ILE PROGRAM SA1D LAST NIGHT HE HAS SEEN NOTHING TO SUGGEST THE RUSSIANS

THE STATEMENT WAS MADE BY MAJe GEN. BERNARD A, SCHRIFVER FOLLOWING 
HIS ARRIVAL FOR A PEARL HARBOR DAY SPEECH TODAY AT NEARBY RICHARDS- 
GEBAUR AIR FORCE BASE. 

SCHRIEVER SAID THE UNITED STATES MAY BE "A YEAR OR TWO" BEHIND RUSSIA 
IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF A SHORT-RANGE MISSILE--ONE WITH A RANGE OF 500 
TO 1,000 MILES. BUT HE SAID THIS TYPE OF MISSILE IS NOT OF PRIMARY 
IMPORTANCE TO THE UNITED STATES 

A SHORT-RANGE MISSILE WOULD BE USEFUL TO RUSSIA BECAUSE IT WOULD BE

THE DEFENSE DEPARTMENT LAST NIGHT MADE AVAILABLE FOR PUBLIC DIS- 
TRIBUTION 900 FEET OF MOTION PICTURE FILM OF THE ABORTIVE VANGUARD 
FIRING. THE FILM, CLEARED BY CENSORS, WAS DESCRIBED BY NEWS PHOTO- 
SRAPHERS AS OF THE HIGHEST QUALITY. 

TAKEN FROM AT LEAST THREE CAMERA POSITIONS AT THE LAUNCHING SITE 
THE FILM SHOWED THE VANGUARD RISE 2 TO 4 FEET OFF ITS PAD, THEN BELCH. - 
RAPIDLY SPREADING BLACK SMOKE AND FIRE FROM ITS BASE. NEWS PHOTO- ° 
SRAPHERS WHO VIEWED THE FILM SAID IT APPEARED THAT THE FIRST STAGE OF» 
THE THREE-STAGE ROCKET WAS QUICKLY CONSUMED IN THE INFERNO SINCE THE C3% . 
VANGUARD SEEMED TO SETTLE BACK TO ITS PAD MORE THAN IT HAD RISEN. 

THE FILM ALSO SHOWS THE NOSE CONE TILTING OFF THE TOP OF THE 
VEHICLE, UNTIL IT SEEMED PARALLEL TO THE GROUND. FROM THAT POINT 
DENSE CLOUDS OF SMOKE AND FLAME OBSCURED THE ENTIRE ROCKET, APPARENTLY 
AS IT TOPPLED OVER ON ITS SIDE.

AMERICAN ATTITUDE OF DEFEATISM WOULD BE REFLECTED IN THE NATO SUMMIT 
“ONFERENCE WHICH OPENS NEXT MONDAY. DEC. 16, IN PARIS.

PRESIDENT EISENHOWER WILL ATTEND. EISENHOWER IS EXPECTED TO GO BUT 
HAS SAID HE WILL SEND NIXON IF HE IS NOT ABLE TO MAKE THE TRIP HIMSELF. 

NIXON SAID HE REGARDS THE PUBLICITY WHICH SURROUNDED THE VANGUARD 
FAILURE AS HARMFUL. 

*3UT THAT IS OUR WAY OF DOING THINGS AND I THINK IT WOULD HAVE BEEN

TRIES THEY MADE FIRST.®

VATICAN CITY, DECe 9 (AP)-THE VATICAN NEWSPAPER L"OSSERVATOR: 
ROMANO WARNED ROMAN CATHOLICS TODAY AGAINST COOPERATING WITH THE 
INTERNATIONAL MORAL REARMAMENT MOVEMENT FOUNDED BY DRe FRANK Ne De 
BUCHMAN. 

THE MOVEMENT. FOUNDED IN 1946, IS DEDICATED TO PEACE AND THE 
BETTERMENT OF MANKIND THROUGH STRENGTHENED MORAL STANDARDS.» 
LYOSSERVATORE SAID CATHOLICS MUST HAVE ®SERIOUS RESERVATIONS" ABOUT 
J h i &amp; 

L'OSSERVATORE SAID THE MOVEMENT HAD BEFOGGED ELEMENTARY RELIGIOUS 
PRINCIPLES AND RECALLED AN INSTRUCTION ISSUED IN 1955 BY THE VATICAN'S 
SUPREME CONGREGATION OF THE HOLY OFFICE, OF WHICH POPE PIUS XII IS 
PREFECT, PROHIBITING PRIESTS FROM ATTENDING CONVENTIONS OF THE MOVEMENT 
AND WARNED CATHOLICS AGAINST ACCEPTING TASKS WITHIN THE MOVEMENT. 

L'OSSERVATORE SAID THE CONGREGATION'S INSTRUCTION STILL *RETAINS 


ALL ITS VALIDITY® INSOFAR AS THE MORAL REARMAMENT MOVEMENT IS 40,57 
CONCERNFD. ; qf.

SPOKESMAN, SAID, "IT'S ALL NEWS TO ME.”

NGTON, DiCe 2 CAF ARNEGIE INSTITUTION OF WASHINGTON SAYS 
et ) W KIND OF WAR--ONE TO BE FOUGHT WITH 
INTELLECTUAL WEAPONS, 


THE INSTITUTION SAID THIS LAST NIGHT IN MAKING PUBLIC THE ANNUAL 
REPORT OF ITS PRESIDENT, DR. CARYL Pe HASKINS, AND ACCOUNTS OF CURRENT 
RESEARCH BY CARNEGIE DEPARTMENTS IN VARIOUS SCIENTIFIC FIELDS RANGING 
FROM ASTRONOMY TO STUDIES OF THE EARTH'S INTERIOR. 

THE INSTITUTION'S STATEMENT SAID “THE RECENT DEMONSTRATIONS OF ” 
RUSSIAN SCIENTIFIC AND TECHNICAL PROWESS UNDERSCORE THE IMPORTANCE 
OF FURTHERING FUNDAMENTAL RESEARCH IN THE NATURAL SCIENCIES. 

"THERE CAN NO LONGER BE DOUBT THAT THE CHALLENGE CONFRONTING THE 
UNITED STATES IS AS URGENT AS _ IT WAS IN 1941," THE STATEMENT SAID. » .. 
"THE CHALLENGE NOW, AS THEN, IS TO TOTAL WAR. hy 

"BUT THIS WAR I$ OF A VERY DIFFERENT KIND, TO BE FOUGHT WITH V 
DIFFERENT WEAPONS. IT WILL NOT BE A WAR OF CLEAN-CUT, SHORT-RUN 
CRISES, TO BE RESOLVED BY OBVIOUS VICTORY OR DEFEAT. It MAY NOT BE 
A WAR FOUGHT ON BATTLEFIELDS, OR WITH WHAT WE THINK OF AS THE NORMAL 
WEAPONS OF WARFARE. IT MAY LAST A GENERATION OR MORE, AND AT TIMES WE 
MAY EVEN FORGET THAT IT IS BEING FOUGHT.® 

THE WEAPONS IN THIS WAR, SAID THE INSTITUTION, "WILL BE TOTAL 
STAMINA AND INTELLECTUAL TONE AND CAPABILITY.® 

“ULTIMATE VICTORY AND PEACE," IT SAID, “WILL BE WON AND MAINTAINED IN 
LARGE MEASURE THROUGH THE LIFE OF THE MIND. 

"THE FUTURE MAY WELL GO TO THAT NATION WHICH SHOWS THE GREATEST 
APPRECIATION AND RESPECT FOR INTELLECTUAL VALUES AND ACCORDS THEM A 
HIGH PLACE IN ITS SOCIETY. THIS IS ESPECIALLY TRUE IN THE FIELD OF 
RESEARCH IN THE NATURAL SCIENCES..."

THIRD NIGHT LEAD MISSILES 
BY VERN HAUGLAND 

CAPE CANAVERAL, FLA., DEC. 10 (AP)-THE ARMY TONIGHT LAUNCHED A 
MODIFIED REDSTONE "TEST VEHICLE*®"--AN EXPERIMENTAL MODEL OF THE TYPE 
WITH WHICH IT PLANS TO PUT A SATELLITE INTO ORBIT AROUND THE EARTH. 

THE FIERY ROCKET SHOT FAR UP INTO SPACE AND WAS VISIBLE FROM 
FLORIDA'S COAST FOR MORE THAN FOUR MINUTES. 

A DEFENSE DEPARTMENT ANNOUNCEMENT SAID "THE LAUNCHING WAS SUCCESSFULS 

THE DEPARTMENT ADDED THAT THE VEHICLE WAS A PART OF THE ARMY'S 
JUPITER PROGRAM. 

THE VEHICLE WITH WHICH THE ARMY PLANS TO LAUNCH A SATELLITE IS 
CALLED THE JUPITER C. IT IS A REDSTONE 200-MILE RANGE MISSILE WITH 
ADDITIONAL ROCKET STAGES FOR REACHING ORBITAL ALTITUDE AND SPEED.

OF THREE STAGES. THERE WAS NO INDICATION, HOWEVER, THAT IT WAS A

THE TWO-DAY SECRET MEETING IS PRELIMINARY TO THE SUMMIT CONFERENCE 
OF NATO OPENING MONDAY. THE UNITED STATES WILL MAKE ITS FORMAL 
OFFER OF INTERMEDIATE RANGE BALLISTICS MISSILES (IRBM) THEN. 

SOME NATO NATIONS ARE RELUCTANT TO ACCEPT THE MISSILES. THE 
OBVIOUS REASON IS A FEAR THEY WILL INVITE SOVIET RETALIATION. AND 
THE MOSCOW PROPAGANDA MACHINE IS PLAYING ON THESE FEARS NOW. 

UsSe MILITARY SOURCES SAID ONLY TWO NATIONS SO FAR HAVE ANNOUNCED 
ACCEPTANCE OF A YEAR-OLD OFFER BY THE UNITED STATES TO SUPPLY NATO 
NATIONS WITH SHORT-RANGE MISSILES CAPABLE OF CARRYING ATOMIC WARHEADS. 

IN THE PAST FEW DAYS, TURKEY AND BELGIUM HAVE FORMALLY ANNOUNCED 
ACCEPTANCE OF THE U.S. OFFERe 

FOR SOME TIME, HOWEVER, ITALY, WEST GERMANY, NORWAY AND DENMARK 
HAVE HAD MISSILE CREWS UNDER TRAINING AT FORT SILL, OKLA., SO THEIR 
COMING ACCEPTANCE IS A FAIR BET, U.S. SOURCES SAID. 

DENMARK AND NORWAY, ON THE NORTHERNMOST FLANK OF THE ALLIANCE 
DEFENSE AREA, HAVE MABE IT CLEAR THEY WILL NOT ACCEPT ANY OFFER 
OF NUCLEAR WARHEADS FOR THE MISSILES. THEY ARE ALSO REPORTED TO BE 
OPPOSED TO TAKING ANY IRBMS. 

WASHINGTON'S ORIGINAL OFFER COVERED ONLY DEFENSIVE MISSILES FOR USE 
AGAINST AIRCRAFT, OR TACTICAL WEAPONS FOR USE AGAINST ENEMY TROOPS 
WITHIN A 250-MILE RADIUS.

CADVANCE) A COMBINATION OF VIOLENT SOVIET AND EGYPTIAN PROPAGANDA 
IS CRYING FOR THE BLOOD OF THE WHITE MAN IN EAST AND CENTRAL AFRICA. 

THE CAMPAIGN IS KEYED TO A CAIRO CONFERENCE OF ASIAN AND AFRICAN 
NATIONS SCHEDULED SOON. THE AIM, BOTH IN MOSCOW AND CAIRO, APPEARS 
TO BE TO GENERATE SEVERE PRESSURE WHICH EVENTUALLY COULD DRIVE THE 
WEST COMPLETELY OUT OF CENTRAL AFRICA, LEAVING THAT STRATEGIC AREA 
CLEAR FOR MOSCOW'S WORLD POLITICAL DRIVE. 

THIS CAMPAIGN PROMISES EVENTUALLY TO STRIKE AT THE WHITE MAN ALL 
THE WAY ACROSS BLACK AFRICA FROM PORTUGUESE ANGOLA TO BRITISH EAST 
AFRICA. 

EVENTUALLY IT COULD ROOT THE WESTERN ALLIES FROM THEIR GUARDIAN 
POSITIONS ASTRIDE SEALANES WHICH ASSURE THE CONTINUED FLOW OF RAW

HOW DOES NUCLEAR FUSION DIFFER FROM FISSION? 
HUGHES EXPLAINS IT THIS WAY: 


marten coe THE ATOM OF AN ELEMENT IS TRANSFORMED INTO ANOTHER FORM OF 


ENERGY IS RELEASED--IF THE PROCESS CAUSES A DECREASE IN THE 
MASS OF MATERIAL INVOLVED. 


SPLITTING OF THE URANIUM NUCLEUS INTO FRAGMENTS IS CALLED FISSION. 
TOGETHER, THE SPLIT FRAGMENTS WEIGH LESS THAN THE ORIGINAL. A SUBSTAN 
TIAL AMOUNT OF MATTER THUS DISAPPEARS. BUT IT REAPPEARS IN THE FORM 


OF ENERGY. 
ENERGY IS ALSO RELEASED WHEN THE ATOMS OF LIGHTER ELEMENTS 


HOWEVER 


ARE FUSED TOCETHER--ALSO WITH A RESULTING LOSS OF WEIGHT, OR MASS. 
THIS IS CALLED NUCLEAR FUSION. AND THE MATTER WHICH DISAPPEARS IN 
THE FUSION PROCESS REAPPEARS IN THE FORM OF ENERGY. 


IT SO HAPPENS, SAYS pp WEIGHT FOR Y sesida te LIGHTER 


ELEMENTS SUCH AS HYBROGEN PRODUCE MORE ENERGY BY FUSION THAN URANIUM 
BOES BY FISSION.

PAL MALETER TO TRIALe 

MALETER WAS THE DEFENSE MINISTER IN THE IMRE NAGY CABINET 
OUSTED BY THE RUSSIANS IN THE 1956 HUNGARIAN REVOLT. HE WAS 
ARRESTED WHILE NEGOTIATING REMOVAL OF SOVIET TROOPS AND TANKS FROM 
BUDAPEST « 

THERE HAVE BEEN FREQUENT REPORTS THAT MALETER HAS BEEN PLACED 
ON TRIAL BY THE GOVERNMENT OF PREMIER JANOS KADAR, WHO WAS INSTALLED 
BY THE RUSSIANS TO SUCCEED NAGY. LAST SATURDAY ROBERT BOROS y 
DEPUTY PRESS CHIEF OF THE HUNGARIAN FOREIGN MINISTRY, DECLINED ANY 
INFORMATION ABOUT MALETER IN A NEWS CONFERENCE HELD IN BUDAPEST. 

RUMORS THAT MALETER IS ON TRIAL WERE REVIVED AGAIN TODAY IN 
DIPLOMATIC CIRCLES IN VIENNA. CORRESPONDENTS NOW BASED IN BUDAPEST 
WERE UNABLE TO CONFIRM THEM. .

UNISIA.

IMMEDIATELY BEFORE THE COUNTDOWN STARTS, THE CREW MEMBERS TAKE 
THEIR STATIONS. ONE BY ONE, THE MEN INFORM THE TEST CONDUCTOR, 
THROUGH AN INTERCOMMUNICATION SYSTEM, THAT THEY ARE READY. 

A DETAILED. STEP BY STEP OPERATION, THE COUNTDOWN SERVES TO 
CHECK COUNTLESS SWITCHES AND VALVES, TO WARM UP AND START MISSILE 
SUBSYSTEMS, TO CHECK THE READINESS OF THE TEST FACILITY AND 
OF RANGE SUPPORTING FUNCTIONS, TO LOAD PROPELLANTS ABOARD THE 
MISSILE, AND FINALLY TO FIRE THE ROCKET ENGINES AND LAUNCH THE 

THE COUNTDOWN SCHEDULE MUST BE FOLLOWED STRICTLY. OPERATORS 
MUST REMAIN AT THEIR STATIONS THROUGH THE COUNTDOWN AND IF A 
MALFUNCTION FORCES A ®HOLD® OR DELAY THE PROCESS CAN LAST MANY 
HOURS. IN CERTAIN TYPES OF "HOLDS", PERSONNEL ARE ALLOWED TO LEAVE 
THEIR POSTS TEMPORARILY. FOOD AND COFFEE ARE ALWAYS AVAILABLE. 

TWO MINUTES BEFORE ZERO, THE BLOCKHOUSE VENTILATION SYSTEM IS 
SHUT OFF IN ORDER TO SEAL THE LAST POSSIBLE INLET FOR FLAME 
MOISTURE OR CAS. EACH OCCUPANT OF THE BUILDING HAS AN AIR PACK 
WHICH CAN SUPPLY OXYGEN IF HE NEEDS IT. 

THE TEST CONDUCTOR PRESSES THE BUTTON THAT STARTS THE ROCKET 
ENGINES. IF, DURING THE BUILDUP OF POWER, HE LEARNS OF ANY 
MALFUNCTION HE CAN CUT OFF THE FIRING BY PRESSING ANOTHER BUTTON. 
IF EVERYTHING IS ALL RIGHT, THE LAUNCHING MECHANISM AUTOMATICALLY 
RELEASES THE MISSILE.

USUALLY WHEN THE EUROPEAN COUNTRIES TALK ABOUT CONSULTATION IN THE 
NORTH ATLANTIC COUNCIL, THEY MEAN CONSULTATION PLUS AGREEMENT. THE 
THEORY IS THAT IF NATIONS CAN TALK OUT THEIR PROBLEMS THEY CAN 
COMPROMISE AND REACH AGREEMENT. BUT THIS DID NOT WORK IN THE CASE 
OF BRITISH-AMERICAN TALKS WITH FRANCE ABOUT SELLING ARMS TO TUNISIA.

SHE NGION, DECe 14 COP) -RUSSIA IS UNDERSTOOD TO HAVE PROTESTED 

TRE Abas AGAINST NAMING A POLISH OFFICIAL TO ONE OF THE TOP POSTS IN 
MSH 60-NATION INTERNATIONAL ATOMIC ENERGY AGENCY CIAEA). 

m@ THE SOVIETS HAVE DEMANDED THAT A RUSSIAN BE APPOINTED INSTEAD TO FILL 
THE SPOT, THAT OF DEPUTY DIRECTOR GENERAL IN CHARGE OF PERSONNEL. 

“DIPLOMATIC INFORMANTS WHO DISLOSED THIS TODAY SAID DIRECTOR GENERAL 
STERLING COLE, FORMER REPUBLICAN CONGRESSMAN FROM NEW YORK, INTENDS TO 
IGNORE THE SOVIET COMPLAINT. 

COLE IS REPORTED WILLING TO NAME ONE RUSSIAN TO A HIGH POST IN THE 
AGENCY BUT IS SAID TO BE UNWILLING TO PICK A SECOND ONE FOR THE TOP 

THE POLE INVOLVED IS REPORTED TO BE KAROL KRACZKIEWICZ, A MEMBER 
OF THE UNITED NATIONS SECRETARIAT WHO IS ON LOAN TO THE NEW AGENCY 
WHICH HAS HEADQUARTERS IN VIENNA. 

THE SOVIETS ARE UNDERSTOOD TO HAVE MADE KNOWN THEIR VIGOROUS 
OBJECTION TO KRACZKIEWICZ"S APPOINTMENT TO AMERICAN AMBASSADOR HENRY 
CABOT LODGE AT U.N. HEADQUARTERS IN NEW YORK. 

RUSSIA'S PROTEST IS VIEWED BY SOME TOP OFFICIALS HERE AS INDICAT- 
ING A DISTRUST IN MOSCOW OF WLADYSLAW GOMULKA'’S POLISH REGIME WHICH IS 
SEEKING MORE INDEPENDENCE FROM THE KREMLIN. 

IAEA WAS FOUNDED IN VIENNA LAST OCTOBER AFTER FOUR YEARS OF PLANN- 
ING. THE AGENCY'S AIM IS TO DEVELOP THE PEACEFUL USES OF ATOMIC ENERGY 
FOR THE BENEFIT OF ALL MANKIND. 

RUSSIA OBJECTED TO NAMING COLE TO THE POST OF DIRECTOR GENERAL BUT 
ABSTAINED INSTEAD OF VOTING AGAINST HIM. THE SOVIETS ARE REPORTED TO 
HAVE OFFERED TO VOTE FOR HIM, PROVIDED THEY WERE ASSURED IN ADVANCE OF 
TWO HIGH POSTS IN THE ORGANIZATION. NEITHER COLE NOR THE STATE DEPART- 
MENT WANTED ANY PART OF SUCH A DEAL. 

TO HELP THE AGENCY GET STARTED, THE UNITED STATES HAS OFFERED TO 
MAKE AVAILABLE 5,000 KILOGRAMS OF URANIUM-235 TO IAEA. RUSSIA HAS 
OFFERED 50 KILOGRAMS AND BRITAIN 20. 

COLE NOW IS IN VIENNA HELPING ORGANIZA A STAFF SO SPECIFIC PROJECTS 
CAN BE UNDERTAKEN BY THE ORGANIZATION EARLY NEXT YEARs soars

THE 37 YEAR OLD AIRMAN FLEW A MCDONNELL F101A VOODOO JET FIGHTER 


AT A SPEED OF 1,207.6 MILES PER HOUR AT EDWAR 


IN HIS VISIT TODAY TO THE AIR SECRETARY 
FLYING est PINNED ON HIM AFTER THE RECORD FLIGHT BY MAJ. GEN. 
CHESTER MCCARTY, COMMANDER OF THE 18TH AIR FORCE. 

DREW TOLD NEWSMEN HE DIDN'T ACTUALLY KNOW HOW FAST HE HAD FLOWN 
UNTIL HE WAS BACK ON THE GROUND, “WHERE I JUMPED OUT AND ASKED THE 
PEOPLE" WHO MADE THE OFFICIAL CHECK ON THE SPEED TRYe HE SAID HE WAS 
AMAZED AND THRILLED" WHEN THE EST OFFICIALS INFORMED HIM HE HAD 


CRACKTN Tur ererapn 


50.24- 15949 


, DREW SAID, THE NEEDLE-NOSED, KNIFE- 
WINGED AIRCRAFT WAS "VERY STABLE, RESPONDING AT ALL TIMES TO CONTROLS 
IN A NORMAL MANNER.® 


DREW HELD THE F101 IN A STRAIGHT AND VIRTUALLY LEVEL COURSE FOR 10 
MILES, VARYING FROM INTENDED ALTITUDE BY NO MORE THAN 50 FEETs 

IN ANSWER TO A QUESTION, HE SAID HE "WOULDN'T HESITATE" TO PUT THE 
vooQ00 INTO A TURN FOR MANEUVERING AT THAT SPEED IF THAT WAS REQUIRED 

HE REPORTED THAT AERODYNAMIC HEATING--THE HEATING OF AN OBJECT FROM 
HIGH SPEED PASSAGE THROUGH THE AIR--BEGAN TO SHOW A LITTLE IN THE 
FLIGHT. PAINTED DECALS ON EITHER WING TIPS WERE BLISTERED BY THE HEAT. 
THE COCKPIT OF THE AIRCRAFT, EVEN AT 39,000 FEET, BEGAN TO WARM ENOUGH 
TO REQUIRE RESETTING OF THE TEMPERATURE CONTROL, DREW SAID. 

DREW, COMMANDER OF THE 4S1ST FIGHTER BOMBER SQUADRON, LIVES WITH HIS 
WIFE AND CHILDREN AT AUSTIN, TEX. HE IS A NATIVE OF CARROLL COUNTY, 

DREW SAID THAT IN THE 45 MINUTES HE WAS IN THE AIR -- WHICH INCLUDED 
TAKEOFF, FLYING QUT ABOUT 50 MILES TO HEAD IN ON THE MEASURED COURSE, 
FLYING THE COURSE ONE WAY AND THEN ANOTHER AND LANDING -- THE AIRCRA 
CONSUMED ABOUT 1,780 GALLONS OF FUEL. AFTERBURNERS TO BOOST THE PUSH 
OF THE TWO 30,000-POUND THRUST PRATT &amp; WHITNEY ENGINES WERE USED AS HE 
MADE THE TWO RUNS. 

THE VOODOO HAS BEEN IN OPERATIONAL SERVICE WITH THE TACTICAL AIR 
COMMAND SINCE LAST MAY. 

IT IS ONE OF THE TWO PRESENT OPERATIONAL JET TYPES OF THE AIR FORCE 
ABLE TO CARRY AND FIRE THE ATOMIC-WARHEADED GENIE ANTIAIRCRAFT ROCKET. 

THE OTHER ROLE OF THE VOODOO IS THAT OF A SWIFT JET BOMBER, FOR 
DELIVERY OF ATOMIC BOMBS AS WELL AS CONVENTIONAL MISSILES AGAINST 
TARGETS ON THE GROUND.

-~PRESIDENT EISENHOWER, ON THE EVE OF NATO'S 
ERENCE; OPENED THE WAY A LITTLE WIDER TODAY FOR EUROPEAN 
ACCEPTANCE OF AMERICAN NUCLEAR MISSILES TO BOLSTER THE ALLIANCE'S 
FRONT LINES AGAINST THE SOVIET THREAT. 

PREPARING FOR NATO'S MOST IMPORTANT ANNUAL SESSION SINCE THE NORTH 
ATLANTIC TREATY ORGANIZATION WAS FOUNDED IN 1949, THE PRESIDENT TACKLED 
THE PRINCIPLE OBSTACLE TO THE MISSILE PLAN--FRANCE, REPRESENTED BY 
PREMIER FELIX GAILLARD» 

IN AN HOUR'S CONSULTATION, HE URGED THE FRENCH, APPARENTLY WITH 
SOME SUCCESS, TO TAKE A WARMER VIEW OF AN AMERICAN OFFER TO PUT INTER- 
MEDIATE RANGE MISSILES AND NUCLEAR WARHEADS ON THE EUROPEAN FRONT 
ACING SOVIET RUSSIA. 

DESPITE THE STRAIN OF TWO DAYS OF PRE-CONFERENCE WORK, THE PRESIDENT 
ALSO POLISHED AND SENT OFF TO INDIA'S PRIME MINISTER NEHRU A TELEGRAM 
ASSURING HIM THE UNITED STATES STILL WANTED DISARMAMENT, BUT COULD NOT 
STOP TESTING NUCLEAR WEAPONS WITHOUT IRONCLAD GUARANTEES. 

THERE WAS A ROUND-ROBIN OF PRIVATE TALKS AMONG TOP LEADERS OF THE 
15-MEMBER ALLIANCE. 

EISENHOWER SAW GAILLARD. GAILLARD LATER SAW WEST GERMAN CHANCELLOR 
KONRAD ADENAUER. ADENAUER MET BRITISH PRIME MINISTER HAROLD MACMILLAN. 


EISENHOWER PLANS TO MEET WITH MACMILLAN BEFORE TOMORROW'S OPENING 
thy THE DRAFTY AND RICKETY NATO BUILDING, THE PALAIS DE

2OMMANDER, ABOUT MEANS OF STRENGTHENING THE WEST'S DEFENSE. HE WENT 
TQ A NATO SERVICE IN THE AMERICAN EPISCOPAL CATHEDRAL NEAR THE SEINE.

TREATY ORGANIZATION THAT HAS BEEN BICKERING AND HEDGING IN THE FACE 
OF RUSSIAN THREATS AND DEMONSTRATIONS OF NEW MILITARY POWER.

ARMISTICE TALKS.

ITE FRENCH BLONDE NAMED SIMONE SERVAIS TODAY 


OPENED UP THE BIGGEST INTERNATIONAL PRESS CENTER IN THE HISTORY OF -MOD-

"I AM VERY GLAD TO SEE YOU," SHE SMILED PRETTILY, *WON'T YOU

FROM 1,867 REPORTERS, PHOTOGRAPHERS, RADIO AND TV MEN AND WOMEN THERE 
WASN'T A SINGLE OBJECTION--A MAJOR MILESTONE IN JOURNALISTIC UNANIMITY. 

MISS SERVAIS IS ASSISTANT PRESS OFFICER FOR THE NATO SUMMIT 
MEETING AND ACTED AS HOSTESS FOR THE OFFICIAL OPENING OF THE 
SPRAWLING PRESS CENTER IN THE PALAIS DE CHAILLOT. 

BUSINESS ACTIVITIES BEGAN WITH NATO SECRETARY GENERAL PAUL-HENRI 
SPAAK OF BELGIUM HOLDING A MASS NEWS CONFERENCE. 

THE FIRST QUESTION WAS ASKED BY A CORRESPONDENT FOR THE FRENCH 
COMMUNIST NEWSPAPER L'HUMANITE. HE ASKED FOR INFORMATION ABOUT NATO'S 

| INFRASTRUCTURE--HIGHLY TOP SECRET STUFF. AN EXPERT PARLIEMENTARIAN, 
SPAAK BRUSHED HIM OFF--BUT POLITELY AND IN FRENCH. 

SIXTY-TWO MINUTES LATER, WHEN THE NEWS CONFERENCE WAS OVER, SPAAK 
WALKED INTO THE BARe HE WAS IMMEDIATELY SURROUNDED BY NEWSMEN. 

THIRTY MINUTES LATER, SPAAK WAS STILL SURROUNDED. BEHIND HIM STOOD 
A PHALANX OF EIGHT FRENCH BARMAIDS WHO OPERATED ON THE PRINCIPLE OF 
SERVING THE LARGEST DRINKS THIS SIDE OF THE SAHARA DESERT. AFTER ALL, 
IT WASN'T THEIR WHISKEY. 

DOWN NEAR ANOTHER BAR MISS SERVAIS WAS SURROUNDED. SHE EXPLAINED 
SWEETLY SHE HAD ISSUED 967 PRESS CARDS TO CORRESPONDENTS REPRESENTING 
450 PAPERS IN 38 COUNTRIES OF THE WORLD. ADDITIONALLY, SHE SAID 
SHE HAD HANDED OUT 900 CARDS TO RADIO COMMENTATORS, PHOTOGRAPHERS AND 
TV MEN AND WOMEN.

nuw IT IS BRINGING AMERICAN HELP TO THOUSANDS OF NEEDY JEWS ARRIVING

AS A FIRST STEP, THE COMMITTEE IS CONCENTRATING ON FOOD FOR CHILDREN. 
TWO THOUSAND FAMILIES ALSO ARE BEING GIVEN BEDDING AND FURNTITURE, 

AND ANOTHER 1,000 PERSONS ARE EXPECTED TO NEED THESE THINGS AS 
REPATRIATION CONTINUES. 

THE AID PROGRAM SPOTLIGHTS THE PLIGHT OF THE JEWISH COMMUNITY WHICH 
BEFORE WORLD WARII NUMBERED 3,500,000 IN A NATION OF 30 MILLION. ABOUT 
3 MILLION DIED IN THE WAR. THOUSANDS MORE ARE SCATTERED AROUND THE 
WORLD. 

IN THE PAST YEAR, 30,000 HAVE LEFT POLAND FOR ISRAEL AND THE WEST. 
ANTI-SEMITISM AND LOW LIVING STANDARDS ARE THE REASONS. 

Now JEWS IN POLAND NUMBER ABOUT 50,000. OF THAT NUMBER, 10,000 CAME 
BACK FROM TH ‘ 4k

WELCOME THE JOINT COMMITTEE'S HELP IN PROVIDING FOR JEWS IN POLAND.

PLAND. HE WORKS WITH JEWISH COMMUNITY LEADERS WHO HAVE SET UP A CENTRAL 
JEWISH COMMITTEE FOR PUBLIC WELFARE. IT HAS SUBCOMMITTEES IN EACH 0 
14 CENTERS WHERE JEWS LIVE IN ANY NUMBERS. MOST ARE IN THE FORMER 
CERMAN WESTERN AREAS. THE BIGGEST COMMUNITY--4,600 PERSONS--IS AT 
LEGNICA, ADVANCE HEADQUARTERS OF SOVIET FORCES IN POLAND AND GERMANY. 

MORE’ THAN HALF THE RETURNING JEWS COME FROM WILNA AND OTHER TOWNS 
THE LITHUANIAN PROVINCES. THE REST COME FROM ALL PARTS OF THE SOVIET 
UNION. WITH A SIZEABLE PROPORTION FROM THE LABOR CAMPS OF SIBERIA. 

ALL WHO RETURN GET CASH CREDITS AND HOUSING AID FROM THE POLISH | 
AUTHORITIES AND A GRANT OF LAND IF THEY WILL ACCEPT IT. BUT MANY 
NOT FARMERS AND WANT TO LIVE IN TOWNS. AS A RESULT ABOUT 15 PER 
CENT ARE UNEMPLOYED. 

THE JOINT COMMITTEE IS GIVING GRANTS TO FINANCE VOCATIONAL 
TRAINING FOR THEM. MANY OTHERS IN TOWNS, JOINT COMMITTEE OFFICIALS

WEAPONS A REE RUSSIA ON GERMAN REUNIFICATION WERE 
URGED TODAY BY THE AMERICAN COUNCIL FOR THE RE-UNIFICATION OF GERMANY. 

THE INDEPENDENT POLITICAL GROUP ISSUED A THREE-POINT RESOLUTION TO 
COINCIDE WITH CURRENT UNITED STATES PARTICIPATION IN THE PARIS 

THE COUNCIL SAID WESTERN GERMANY SHOULD BE EXEMPTED FROM ANY 
NATO DECISION TO EQUIP OUR EUROPEAN ALLIES WITH NUCLEAR WEAPONS. 

"ATOMIC ARMS FOR WESTERN GERMANY WOULD MOST PROBABLY RENDER 
CERMAN RE-UNIFICATION IMPOSSIBLE AND THUS DEFEAT A MAJOR FOREIGN 
POLICY AIM OF THE Ue Se", THE RESOLUTION READ. 

"AMERICA MUST NOT SACRIFICE A LONG TERM POLICY GOAL FOR TEM- 
PORARY MILITARY ADVANTAGES IN EUROPE." 

THE COUNCIL SAID "NEW TOP LEVEL NEGOTIATIONS WITH THE SOVIET UNION 
SHOULD BE SOUGHT ON THE SUBJECT OF MUTUAL TROOP WITHDRAWAL FROM GER- 
MANY AND SUBSEQUENT REUNIFICATION OF THAT COUNTRY»" 

RICHARD Es. SPERBER. COUNCIL CHAIRMAN, SAID THE GROUP SUPPORTED SUCH 
PROPOSALS "LONG BEFORE SOVIET PREMIER BULGANIN CAME OUT WITH A 
SIMILAR PROPOSALS FEW DAYS ACO.

-NIKITA KHRUSHCHEV IN A MAGAZINE ARTICLE TODAY 
RAISED TRE SPECTER DESTRUCTION FOR ANY WEST EUROPEAN NATION 
ALLOWING AMERICAN ATOMIC BASES ON ITS TERRITORY. a 

AT THE SAME TIME HE SAID HE WANTS MEETINGS QF SOVIET AND AMBRIS™ 
LEADERS TO "DISCUSS CONDITION , i nities 

THE SOVIET COMMUNIST PARTY BOSS SAID COUNTRIES WHICH ACCEPT AMERICAN 
ATOMIC BASES FACE "SHATTERING RETALIATORY ATTACKS" IN THE EVENT OF A 
WAR LAUNCHED AGAINST RUSSIA AS A RESULT OF A MISUNDERSTOOD ORDER 
OR AT THE DISCRETION OF SOME AMERICAN OFFICER. | 

"THE COLD WAR AND THE ARMS DRIVE WILL LEAD TO A_NEW AND VERY 
BLOODY WAR," KHRUSHCHEV WARNED IN A LETTER PUBLISHED BY THE NEW 
STATESMAN. A LEFTISH WEEKLY REVIEW. c 
"HIS LETTER SEEMED DESIGNED TO PLAY ON THE FEARS OF SEVERAL 
EUROPEAN GOVERNMENT LEADERS NOW IN PARIS WITH PRESIDENT EISENHOWER 
AT THE NATO SUMMIT CONFERENCE WHERE THE BUILDING OF U.S. NUCLEAR 
MISSILE BASES IN EUROPE HAS BEEN AGREED TO ONLY IN PRINCIPLE. 

"NUCLEAR WEAPONS, BROUGHT FROM ACROSS THE OCEAN, ARE IMPOSED _ 

ON WEST EUROPEAN MEMBER STATES OF NATO UNDER THE GUISE OF DEFENSE 
AGAINST AGGRESSION." KHRUSHCHEV SAID. . 

"IN REALITY THE DEPLOYMENT OF NUCLEAR WEAPONS ON THE TERRITORIES 
OF THESE COUNTRIES IS A MORTAL BLOW TO THEIR SECURITY. 

"IF AN AGGRESSOR BREAKS THE PEACE, THEN, IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE 
INEXORABLE LOGIC OF WAR, SHATTERING RETALIATORY ATTACKS ON THE 
TERRITORIES OF THOSE COUNTRIES IN WHICH ATOMIC BASES ARE SITUATED 
WILL BE INEVITABLE.® 

KHRUSHCHEV WROTE TO THE NEW STATESMAN IN REPLY TO AN OPEN LETTER BY 
THE BRITISH PHILOSOPHER BERTRAND RUSSELL, AN EARL WHO NEVER USES HIS 

RUSSELL, WHO ADDRESSED HIS OPEN LETTER BOTH TO KHRUSHCHEV AND 
PRESIDENT EISENHOWER, HAD APPEALED FOR A UeSe-SOVIET ACCORD BASED 
ON f\ DECLARATION THAT NEITHER POWER WOULD SEEK TO SPREAD ITS CREED

BY DAVID MASON | 

BAR &gt; (AP)-SECRETARY OF STATE BULLES DECLARED TODAY THE 
HISTORIC NATO SUMMIT CONFERENCE HAB "GONE A LONG WAY TO ACCEPT A 
STRATEGY OF VICTORY® OVER THE SOVIET THREAT. 

THE SECRETARY OF STATE SAID THE ®°STRATEGY OF VICTORY® DECIDED UPON 
WAS TWO-FOLD--"TAKING ACCOUNT OF THE FORMIDABLE STRENGTH (OF THE 
RUSSIANS) AND EXPLOITING THE WEAKNESS OF THOSE ARRAYED AGAINST US. 

THE NATO CHIEFS OF STATE BECIDED TO REINFORCE THE ALLIANCE'S

NORWAY WHILE THERE IS A CHANCE OF NEGOTIATING WITH THE SOVIET __ 

UNION. EARLIER NORWAY ACCEPTED HONEST JOHN GROUND-TO-GROUND MISSILES. 

THE SOURCE SAID MILITARY LEADERS AGREE THAT NORWEGIAN FORCES IN THE 
STRATEGIC NORTHERN NORWAY COULD NOT POSSIBLY HOLD UNTIL ALLIED AID 
IS AVAILABLE, UNLESS THE FEW SMALL UNITS IN THE AREA ARE EQUIPPED WITH 
ATOMIC MISSILES. 

THE SOURCE ADDED THAT MILITARY LEADERS HERE INTERPRET THE 
NORWEGIAN STAND AT PARIS AS MEANING THAT FROM THE MILITARY POINT OF 
VIEW NORWAY AND DENMARK WILL ABSTAIN FROM THE SECURITY INHERENT IN 
NATO"S DEFENSE SYSTEM. 

THE SHORT-RANGE MISSILE AND ATOMIC WAR HEAD PLAN MAY BE A 
COMPROMISE BETWEEN THE NECESSITY OF DEFENDING NORWEGIAN SOIL 
AND THE BASE POLICY OF THE NORWEGIAN GOVERMENT . THE SOURCE SAID.

DAY SIGNED A CONVENTION CREATING A EUROPEAN NUCLEAR ENERGY AGENCY TO 


PROMOTE TECHNICAL COOPERATION IN PEACEFUL ATOMIC DEVELOPMENT. 

THE NATIONS THAT FORMALLY RATIFIED AN AGREEMENT REACHED SEVERAL 
MONTHS AGO INCLUDED ALL OF THOSE IN THE ORGANIZATION FOR EUEUROP- 
EAN ECONOMIC COOPERATION (OFEC) EXCEPT IRELANDe IRELAND DID NOT 
SIGN BECAUSE OF A TECHNICALITY BUT WAS EXPECTED TO JOIN LATER. 

SIX OF THE 16 NATIONS ARE UNITED IN A POLLED EFFORT TO DEVELOP 
NUCLEAR POWER. IN THE ORGANIZATION CALLED EURATOM ARE FRANCE, 

WEST GERMANY, ITALY, THE NETHERLANDS, BELGIUM AND LUXEMBOURG. 

TWELVE OF THE OEEC COUNTRIES ALSO SIGNED AN AGREEMENT SETTING UP 
THE FIRST INDUSTRIAL ENTERPRISE IN EUROPE TO BE JOINTLY EXPLOITED 
BY GOVERNMENTS. THIS IS THE EUROCHEMIC CORP., WHICH WILL RUN A 
PLUTONIUM FACTORY IN BELGIUM. 

BESIDES THE EURATOM SIX AND IRELAND, OTHER OEEC NATIONS ARE 
BRITAIN, NORWAY, DENMARK, ICELAND, SWEDEN, PORTUGAL, GREECE, TURKEY, : 
AUSTRIA AND SWITZERLAND.

OF THE NATIONS MET TODAY TO DISCUSS A HEADQUARTERS CITY FOR THE TWO 
ORGANIZATIONS, THEY DECIDED TO MAKE THEIR SELECTION AT A MEETING

DOUGLAS HAS BEEN ON A ONE-MAN FACT-FINDING MISSION TO STUDY

MARKET--DUE TO COME INTO OPERATION NEXT MONTH--WOULD BRING GREAT

BUT IT COULD HAVE A DAMAGING EFFECT @N AMERICA’S FOREIGN 
TRADE UNLESS THE UNITED STATES MAINTAINS ITS ACTIVE AND PROMINENT 
MEMBERSHIP @F THE GENERAL AGREEMENT ON TARIFFS AND TRADE (GATT), HE 
SAID. THE RECIPROCAL TRADE AGREEMENTS ACT IS THE BASIS FOR AMERICAN 
GATT MEMBERSHIP. 

"THERE IS ALWAYS A BANGER THAT (THE COMMON MARKET) MAY IMPOSE

SUCH QUOTAS BY STAYING IN GATT.® 

AS AN EXAMPLE OF THE POSSIBLE EFFECTS OF THE COMMON MARKET,

NETHERLANDS. UNLESS THE UNITED STATES WERE ABLE TO OFFER TARIFF 
REDUCTIONS IN COMPENSATION, IT WOULD BE DIFFICULT TO PREVENT 
THESE TWO COUNTRIES SWITCHING MUCH OF THEIR WHEAT PURCHASES FROM THE 
UNITED STATES TO FRANCE, HE SAID. 

HE SAID HE FAVORED A LARGE-SCALE ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT PROGRAM

VALLEYS OF IRAQ, PALESTINE AND EGYPT. SUCH A DEVELOPMENT WOULD PERMIT

FOREIGN AID FOR SUCH A PURPOSE, DOUGLAS SAID “THE COST OF SUCH A 
PROJECT WOULD BE INFINITELY SMALLER THAN THE COST OF A WAR-~AND

A HUNGARIAN CHURCH PERLODICAL EARLY THIS WEEK DISCLOSED THAT 
“HURCH-ELECTED LEADERS ARE BEING REPLACED BY APPOINTEES OF THE 
“OMMUNIST GOVERNMENT. | 

THIS HAS PRODUCED UNEASY REPERCUSSIONS IN THE HEADQUARTERS OF WORLD 
CHURCH BODIES, WHICH HAD BEEN HOPEFUL THE NEW FREEDOMS GAINED 
BY THE HUNGARIAN CHURCH LATE IN 1956 WOULD BE CONTINUED. 

TKE REV. DR. FRANKLIN CLARK FRY, PRESIDENT OF THE LUTHERAN WORLD 
FEDERATION. SAID IT IS "IMPOSSIBLE TO OVERSTATE THE SHOCK AND ANXIETY 
SAUSED BY THE NEW DEVELOPMENTS. . 

HE SAID THE FEDERATION, REPRESENTING 61 CHURCH BODIES WITH 50 
MILLION MEMBERS IN 32 COUNTRIES, "STRONGLY PROTESTS" THE ACTION — 

BY THE HUNGARIAN GOVERNMENT AND "URGENTLY CALLS FOR ITS REVERSAL. 

"CHRISTIAN CONGREGATIONS THEMSELVES MUST ALWAYS HAVE THE 
PREVAILING VOICE, WITE GUIDANCE OF THE HOLY SPIRIT, IN THE CHOICE OF 


THEIR OWN LEADERSHIP," HE SAID. 
OTHERWISE, HE ADDED, "THE CHURCH, INSTEAD OF BEING GOD'S, IS 
6 BEC + IN THE HANDS OF SOMEBODY ELSE,

IN GENEVA, THE REV. DR. WeAs VISSER 'T HOOFT, GENERAL SECRETARY 
OF THE WORLD COUNCIL OF CHURCHES, SAID THE "HUNGARIAN CHURCHES 
SHOULD BE GIVEN FULL FREEDOM IN CHOOSING THE LEADERS THEY DESIRE." 

AFTER THE AUTUMN REVOLUTION OF 1956 IN HUNGARY, MANY PASTORS AND 
PRELATES LONG REBUFFED BY THE HUNGARIAN COMMUNIST REGIME WERE 
ALLOWED TO RESUME CHURCH OFFICES AT THE DISCRETION OF CHURCH SYNODS. 

THIS TREND FIRED HOPES OF A FREER HUNGARIAN CHURCH, AND LUTHERANS 
IN AMERICAN AND ELSEWHERE BEGAN MAKING PLANS TO SEND LARGE-SCALE 
FINANCIAL AID TO THE CHURCHES THERE. , | 

HOWEVER, THE DEC. 15 ISSUE OF EVANGELIKUS ELET, WEEKLY PERIODICAL 
OF THE HUNGARIAN LUTHERAN CHURCH, SAID LEADERS ELECTED BY THE CHURCH 
SYNOD HAD BEEN DISPLACED BY APPOINTEES OF THE COMMUNIST REGIME. 

AMONG THE CHANGES WERE THE RETURN OF BISHOP LAJOS VETO AS HEAD 
OF THE CHURCH'S NORTHERN DISTRICT. THIS GOVERNMENT-SPONSORED 
BISHOP HAD BEEN FORCED OUT IN THE 1956 UPRISING, AND REPLACED BY 
CHURCH-ELECTED BISHOP ZOLTAN TUROCZY, WHO IS NOW OUT AGAIN. 

THERE WAS NO WORD IN THE LATEST SHAKEUPS ABOUT BISHOP LAJOS 
ORDASS » PRESIDING BISHOP OF THE CHURCH RESTORED TO OFFICE IN 1956, 
AFTER EIGHT YEARS OF IMPRISONMENT AND HOUSE ARREST. 

BUT WESTERN LEADERS SAW OMINOUS SIGNS CONCERNING HIM. IT WAS 
NOTED HIS NAME WAS REMOVED FROM THE MASTHEAD OF THE ISSUE OF 
EVANGELIKUS ELET REPORTING THE NEW CHANGES. 

THE REVe DRe CARL Eo LUND-QUIST, EXECUTIVE SECRETARY OF THE LWF, 
SAID IN GENEVA THAT BISHOP ORDASS, WHOM HE VISITED IN NOVEMBER, 
RECOGNIZED FOR SOME TIME THAT A CRISIS WOULD DEVELOP. ® . 
. "BUT UNTIL NOW THE STATE HAD BEEN WILLING TO NEGOTIATE WITH HIM. 

Re VISSER "T HOOFT SAID THE WORLD COUNCIL, REPRESENTING 165 _ 
PRO ESTANT, ORTHODOX AND ANGLICAN DENOMINATIONS IN 50 NATIONS 
SUPPORTS BISHOP ORDASS AND ALL OTHERS IN HUNGARIAN CHURCHES WHO 
STAND FOR FREEDOM OF THE CHURCH.®

THESE FINDINGS BECAME APPARENT FROM A RUNNING SERIES OF TALKS WITH 
EUROPEAN DIPLOMATS BEFORE, DURING AND AFTER THE CONFERENCE. AT THE 
CONFERENCE AN AGREEMENT IN PRINCIPLE WAS REACHED TO STOCKPILE EUROPE 
WITH NUCLEAR WEAPONS--BUT ONLY AFTER AN ATTEMPT IS MADE TO GET RUSSIA 
INTO A CONFERENCE ON DISARMAMENT AND OTHER SUBJECTS ENDANGERING PEACEe 

A FUNDAMENTAL DIFFERENCE IN POINT OF VIEW BETWEEN DULLES AND SOME 
OF THE EUROPEAN FOREIGN MINISTERS THUS WAS MADE RELATIVELY APPARENT. 
DULLES CLEARLY DISLIKES TALKING TO THE RUSSIANS BECAUSE HE FEELS IT IS 
FRUITLESS. EUROPEANS SUPPOSE THAT A GREAT MANY AMERICANS ALSO_FEEL 
THAT DEALING WITH COMMUNIST POWERS IS A SORDID AND DIRTY BUSINESS WHICH 
A CLEAN MINDED COUNTRY OUGHT TO AVOID. 

EUROPEANS FOR THE MOST PART DON'T LIKE COMMUNISM BUT DON'T SHARE 
THE FEELING OF MANY AMERICANS THAT IT IS A CONTAGION TO BE AVOIDED. 


THIS IS AN IMPORTANT DIFFERENCE OF ATTITUDE. WHILE EUROPEANS FEEL 
THE LATE PRESIDENT ROOSEVELT WENT MUCH TOO FAR IN DEALING WITH THE 
RUSSIANS AND TRUSTING TKEM, THEY FEEL DULLES IS FAR TOO SUSPICIOUS. 

IT IS ON THIS FRONT FIRST THAT EUROPEAN DIPLOMATS ARE LIKELY TO 
EXERT THEIR EARLIEST AND MOST URGENT PRESSURE. 

THEY FEEL THAT AGREEMENT BY THE AMERICANS TO ANY TALKS AT ALL 
WITH THE RUSSIANS WAS A GAIN, ALTHOUGH THEY OVERLOOK SOMEWHAT THAT 
AMERICA TRIED TO FIND A FORMULA FOR CONTINUING DISARMAMENT TALKS 
WHICH THE RUSSIANS, BUOYANT ABOUT THEIR SPUTNIKS, BOLTED IN DISDAIN. 

EUROPEANS, NOTABLY FRENCH AND GERMANS, FEEL GAINS WERE MADE AT 
THE SUMMIT TALKS. RELUCTANTLY, THEY GAVE IN TO THE AMERICANS “IN 
PRINCIPLE® ABOUT BOMBS AND MISSILES BUT THEY GOT THE AMERICANS TO 
GIVE WAY ON THE URGENCY OF TALKS WITH RUSSIA. TO THAT EXTENT, BOTH 
SIDES GAINED, BOTH SIDES WERE LEFT MODERATELY HAPPY. 

"WE ARE NOT TOO UNHAPPY ABOUT THE OUTCOME," SAID A FRENCH 
SOURCE. “IT MIGHT HAVE BEEN A DEADLOCK," AND HE IMPLIED THAT WOULD 
HAVE BEEN CATASTROPHIC FOR THE NATO ALLIANCE. 

UNDER THE CONFERENCE AGREEMENT, ALL COUNTRIES CONCEDED NUCLEAR 
MISSILE BASES WERE NEEDED IN WESTERN EUROPE. THE NORTH ATLANTIC 
TREATY COMMANDER AND THE NATO DEFENSE COMMITTEE WILL DECIDE WHERE 
MISSILE BASES ARE NEEDED TO REINFORCE THE WEST'S WEAK LINE FACING 
RUSSIA. AFTER THAT, EACH COUNTRY CHOSEN AS A SITE WILL NEGOTIATE 
WITH THE UNITED STATES ON CONDITIONS FOR ESTABLISHMENT OF SUCH SITES 
AND NUCLEAR STORES. f

CHIEF JUSTICE JOZSEF DOMONKOS DISCLOSED IN ANOTHER SPEECH THAT MORE 
THAN HALF HIS JUDGES HAD BEEN FIRED FOR REFUSING TO JOIN SUMMARY 
COURTS SET UP AFTER THE REBELLION WAS CRUSHED. IT WAS NOT 
IMMEDIATELY CLEAR IF HE WAS REFERRING TO THE SUPREME COURT ALONE, OR 
TO ALL JUDGES. THE LINE BETWEEN COURTS IS A VAGUE ONE FROM THE 
WESTERN VIEWPOINT, WITH LOWER COURT JUDGES FREQUENTLY BEING CALLED 
TO SERVE ON THE SUPREME BENCH. he 

THE SUMMARY COURTS WERE EMPOWERED TO IMPOSE DEATH SENTENCES, TO BE 
EXECUTED IN 24 HOURS WITHOUT APPEAL, FOR SUCH OFFENSES AS ENTERING A 
FACTORY TO URGE A STRIKEe LAYMEN SAT ON THESE COURTS ALONGSIDE 
PROFESSIONAL JUDGES. 

AN AUTHORITATIVE COMMUNIST SOURCE SAID TODAY THE CASE OF MAJs GEN. 
PAL MALETER, REBEL HERO OF THE 1956 UPRISING, HAD NOT YET REACHED 
COURT. IT WAS SAID TO BE STILL UNDER INVESTIGATION. 

THE PROSECUTOR SAID THAT AS OF YESTERDAY, THERE WERE ONLY 1,869 
HUNGARIANS UNDER "DETENTION FOR REASONS OF PUBLIC SECURITY." __ 

HE ADDED THAT ONLY ONE CAMP NOW EXISTS--PRESUMABLY THE ONE AT THE 
SOVIET MILITARY AIRPORT WHERE MALETER WAS ARRESTED WHILE NEGOTIATING THE 
WITHDRAWAL OF SOVIET TROOPS WITH RED ARMY LEADERS. 

JUSTICE DOMONKOS GAVE SOME FIGURES ON THE NUMBER OF CASES ARISING 
FROM THE "COUNTER-REVOLUTION." HE SAID THAT UP TO NOV. 30 THE

TO THE SOVIETS.

SAID THAT ONCE RUSSIA IS ABLE TO KNOCK OUT THE BOMBERS OF THE 
STRATEGIC AIR COMMAND (SAC), THE "CHIEF DETERRENT TO WORLD WAR III" 


WILL HAVE BEEN LOST.

IMMEDIATELY CONVERT AT LEAST 13 CONVENTIONAL SUBMARINES TO CARRY AND 
FIRE MISSILES. HE URGED FURTHER THAT 50 NUCLEAR-POWERED SUBS,

WASHINGTON, DEC. 23 (AP)-THE COUNTRY’S FIRST FULL SCALE NUCLEAR POWR 
PLANT FOR CIVILIAN USE REACHED FULL POWER AT SHIPPINGPORT, PAs, TODAY, 
THE ATOMIC ENERGY COMMISSION AND THE DUQUESNE LIGHT CO. ANNOUNCED. 


THE JOINT ANNOUNCEMENT SAID THE PLANT DELIVERED, ON A TEST BASIS, 
APPROXIMATELY 60,000 KILOWATTS OF ELECTRICITY--THE EXPECTED INITIAL 
CAPACITY OF THE PLANT--TO THE DUQUESNE COMPANY'S TRANSMISSION SYSTEM IN 
THE PITTSBURGH AREA. 


THE PLANT FIRST BEGAN PUSHING ELECTRICITY INTO THE DUQUESNE SYSTEM 
ON A LESSER SCALE ON DEC. 18. 

THE 60,000 KILOWATTS CAPACITY OF THE PLANT IS ENOUGH ELECTRICITY TO 
SUPPLY TO NEEDS OF A RESIDENTIAL COMMUNITY OF 250,000 PERSONS. 

THE SHIPPINGPORT OUTPUT IS ONLY A FRACTION OF THE DUQUESNE COMPANY'S 
TOTAL GENERATING CAPACITY OF SOME 1 1/4 MILLION KILOWATTS. 

THE AEC-DUQUESNE ANNOUNCEMENT SAID? 

THE TURBINE-GENERATOR PRODUCED 68,000 KILOWATTS, THE DIFFERENCE OF 
8,000 KILOWATTS BEING REQUIRED FOR THE STATION'S OWN SERVICE~ 5,500 
KILOWATTS OF ELECTRICITY 1S REQUIRED TO OPERATE THREE OF TH TOR 
CIRCULATING PUMPS AND 2,500 KILOWATTS IS REQUIRED FOR OTHER 
LIGHTING, AND MISCELLANEOUS PURPOSES. 

"THE SHIPPINGPORT REACTOR, AT ITS NET POWER LEVEL OF 60,000 
KILOWATTS WAS PRODUCING MORE ELECTRICITY THAN ANY OTHER INDIVIDUAL 
REACTOR IN EXISTENCE.® 

WESTINGHOUSE ELECTRIC CORP. BUILT THE NUCLEAR REACTOR UNDER 
CONTRACT WITH THE ATOMIC ENERGY COMMISSION. DUQUESNE CONTRIBUTED

EASTERN EUROPE 


FOREIGN CORRESPONDENTS WITHIN THE EAST EUROPEAN COMMUNIST 
SPHERE OPERATE UNDER A CENSORSHIP OF RESPONSIBILITY. THERE IS_ NO 
DIRECT CHECK ON DISPATCHES FILED BY THE FEW WESTERNERS pith 
BUT THE COMMUNISTS SCAN THE REPORTS PUBLISHED ABROAD AND CAN FORCE 
THE DEPARTURE OF CORRESPONDENTS WHO OFFEND THEM. 

WITH THE EXCEPTION OF POLAND, VISAS FOR THAT AREA HAVE BEEN 
SCANT SINCE THE HUNGARIAN REVOLT OF 1956. THE EASIEST WAY TO GET 
A VISA IS TO APPLY TO COVER A SPORTS EVENT. ety he Fe THE PRINCIPAL 
WESTERN NEWS AGENCIES AND SOME NEWSPAPERS MAINTAIN CORRESPONDENTS IN 
WARSAW. 

SOURCE CENSORSHIP AFFECTS NEWSMEN THROUGHOUT THE AREA. 

DOMESTIC PRESS AND RADIO OUTLETS ARE TIGHTLY CONTROLLED. 
SOMETIMES THIS IS DIRECT, AS IN POLAND. SOMETIMES IT IS ACHIBVb)~., 
THROUGH SUPPRESSION OF "UNSUITABLE" ARTICLES BY COMMUNIST PARTY. V4 
REPRESENTATIVES SERVING AS EDITORS, AS IN HUNGARY AND YUGOSLAVIA. ®. 

HUNGARIANS MAY BE JAILED FOR PUBLICATION OF NEWS THE COMMUNIST 
GOVERNMENT CONSIDERS UNSATISFACTORY. HOWEVER, PRESS POLICY WHICH 
TIGHTENED AFTER COLLAPSE OF THE 1956 REBELLION HAS BEGUN TO EASE 
Se EAST GERMANY HAS BEEN TIGHTER THAN MOST OTHER SOVIET SATELLITES 
IN REFUSING VISAS TO WESTERN WRITERS. PUBLICATION OF UNAUTHORIZED 
INFORMATION IS A CRIMINAL OFFENSE THERE.

WESTERN EUROPE 


PRESS FREEDOM IS THE RULE IN WESTERN EUROPE, FROM SCANDINAVIA 
TO THE MEDITERRANEAN. 


E

TURKEY AND THE MIDDLE EAST 

CENSORSHIP IS GENERAL IN THE MIDDLE EAST, WHERE TENSION BETWEEN 
TURKEY AND SYRIA WAS A HIGHLIGHT OF THE CLOSING YEAR. en 

TURKEY'S PRESS LAWS ADD UP TO HIDDEN CENSORSHIP. THEY PROVI 
PENALTIES UP TO A 3-YEAR PRISON TERM AND FINE OF 10,000 TURKISH POUNDS 
(3,571) FOR SUCH THINGS AS BELITTLING OFFICIALS OR PUBLISHING FAL 
NEWS DAMAGING TO THE NATION'S FINANCIAL STANDING, PUBLIC ORDER OR 
SECURITY. FOUR JOURNALISTS HAVE BEEN JAILED (BUT SINCE FREED) AND 
MANY OTHERS INDICTED. NO FOREIGN CORRESPONDENTS HAVE BEEN AFFECTED. 

PREMIER ADNAN MENDERES' REGIME THIS FALL ISSUED TWO NEW DECREES 
TENDING TO BRING THE PRESS UNDER FURTHER CONTROL. THE FIRST CREATED 
A NEW GOVERNMENTAL AGENCY TO CHANNEL ALL ADVERTISING TO NEWSPAPERS 
AND DETERMINE THE SIZE AND PROPORTION OF ADS. THE SECOND PLACED 
IMPORT AND DISTRIBUTION OF NEWSPRINT UNDER GOVERNMENT CONTROL. 

THE SITUATION IN THE ARAB SPHERE APPEARS TO HAVE WORSENED. 

SYRIA'S ENTIRE PRESS IS RIGIDLY CONTROLLED BY BOTH THE GOVERNMENT 
AND THE MILITARY. THE GOVERNMENT DENIES CENSORSHIP OF FOREIGN 
DISPATCHES, BUT THERE IS EVIDENCE OF SPOT CHECKS AND DELAY OF 7

CENSORSHIP UNDER MARTIAL LAW ARISING FROM AN APRIL CRISTSE $s ie 

ELSEWHERE THE SITUATION RANGES FROM LEBANON'S RELATIVE ARODERATE 
APPROACH TO SAUDI ARABIA'S TIGHT CONTROL OF THE DOMESTIC PRESS 
AND RELUCTANCE TO ADMIT FOREIGN NEWSMEN.

ATHENS, GREECE, DEC. 23 (AP)-THE GREEK GOVERNMENT UNDERTOOK TODAY 
TO REPAIR ALL DAMAGE DONE TO U.Se PROPERTY IN BOMBINGS HERE DEC 13. 

THE FOREIGN MINISTRY INFORMED U.S. CHARGE D'AFFAIRES JAMES PENFIELD 
OF THIS AND GAVE HIM A REPORT ON GREEK INVESTIGATIONS OF THE BOMBINGS. 
THE REPORT WAS NOT DISCLOSED. 

BOMBS WRECKED THE U.S. INFORMATION SERVICE LIBRARY IN ATHENS 
ae ue AIRPORT. PLANT OUT OF COMMISSION AT A U.S. SECTOR OF THE

MAY HAVE BEEN IN REPLY TO THE U.S. REJECTION IN THE UNITED NATIONS

LONDON, DEC. 24 CAP)&lt;FOREIGN SECRETARY SELWYN LLOYD SAID LAST NIGHT 
THE POLISH PROPOSAL TO BAR NUCLEAR WEAPONS FROM CENTRAL EUROPE COULD 

PROVIDE A STARTING POINT FOR DISARMAMENT TALKS WITH THE RUSSIANS. 

BUT LLOYD TOLD A TELEVISION INTERVIEWER THE SOVIET PROPOSALS FOR 
WITHDRAWAL OF EAST-WEST ARMIES FROM CENTRAL EUROPE HAVE LITTLE MEANING 
IN THE MISSILE ACE. 

"WITH WEAPONS WITH RANGES OF 4,000 MILES OR MORE," HE DECLARED, *THE 
FUTURE OF THE STRIP OF GROUND IN THE MIDDLE IS OF MUCH LESS IMPORTANCE. 

LLOYD CAUTIONED THAT THE WEST, IN FUTURE NEGOTIATIONS WITH THE 
SOVIETS, MUST KEEP ITS GUARD UP AND SEE THAT ITS ALLIANCES ARE NOT 
JEOPARDIZED. 

HE SAID THE POLISH PROPOSAL TO KEEP NUCLEAR ARMS OUT OF EAST AND WEST 
GERMANY, POLAND AND CZECHOSLOVAKIA SHOULD BE EXAMINED "VERY CAREFULLY 
AS ONE OF THE DISARMAMENT PROPOSALS."

WASHINGTON, DEC. 25 (AP)-A SPLIT APPEARS TO BE DEVELOPING AMONG 
TOP ADMINISTRATION OFFICIALS WHO ARE TRYING TO DECIDE HOW THE ATLANTIC 
ALLIES SHOULD NEGOTIATE WITH RUSSIA TO EASE THE INTERNATIONAL DISARMA- 

THIS BACKSTAGE TUSSLE MAY BE CARRIED ALL THE WAY TO PRESIDENT 
EISENHOWER BEFORE THE ADMINISTRATION LAYS DOWN STRATEGY THAT WILL GUIDE 
IT IN A NEW ROUND OF TALKS WITH THE SOVIETS. 

MOST TOP OFFICIALS BELIEVE THE NEXT AMERICAN STEP SHOULD BE TO 
PROPOSE THAT RUSSIA PROVE ITS PEACEFUL INTENT BY MOVING INTO SERIOUS 
DISARMAMENT NEGOTIATION IN THE NEWLY CREATED UNITED NATIONS DISARMA- 
MENT COMMISSION, 

SUCH A MOVE WOULD BE IN KEEPING, THEY SAID, WITH PRESIDENT EISEN- 
HOWER'S CHALLENGE TO RUSSIA'S LEADERS TO DEMONSTRATE "CLEAR EVIDENCE 
OF INTEGRITY.® Rey

NIGHT SUMMING UP THE RESULTS OF THE PARIS ATLANTIC PACT MEETING.

FORCE WAS A VERY DISTINCT EXPRESSION OF INTERNATIONAL COOPERATION, AND |

WAS PLEASED WITH THE SPIRIT OF CQMRADESHIP.

THE INTERNATIONAL COMMUNITY.

ONG KONG. DEC )-LO LUNG-CHIL, RED CHINA'S TIMBER INDUSTRY 
REPOR SED TODAY TO HAVE BEEN PRESSURED ANEW TO ADMIT TO 

SO-CALLED ®RIGHTIST® ACTIVITIES. BUT THE NEW CHINA NEWS AGENCY QUOTED 

HIM AS REPLYING DEFIANTLY: 

"THERE ARE SOME THINGS I WILL NEVER CONFESS TO EVEN THOUGH IT 
MEANS DEATH TO ME.® 

THE AGENCY SAID THE AMERICAN-EDUCATED OFFICIAL WAS BITTERLY 
CRITICISED BY THE CENTRAL COMMITTEE OF THE NON-COMMUNIST DEMOCRATIC 
LEAGUE IN FORUMS LAST WEEKEND. LO IS VICE CHAIRMAN OF THE LEAGUE. 

HE ADMITTED TO "CRIMES AGAINST THE COMMUNIST PARTY AND SOCIALISM,® 
THE AGENCY SAID, "BUT STUBBORNLY DENIED HAVING CARRIED OUT ANY 
CONCRETE ACTIVITIFS.® 

THE AGENCY CLAIMED LO HAD PLOTTED TO SEIZE LEADERSHIP TO COMMUNIST 
CHINA'S ESTIMATED FIVE MILLION INTELLECTUALS. LO AND OTHER RIGHTISTS 
HAVE BEEN UNDER SHARP ATTACK FOR QUESTIONING THE COMMUNISTS’ RIGHT TO 
RULE CHINA, BUT THEY HAVE NOT BEEN REMOVED FROM THEIR JOBS. ANOTHER 
OFFICIAL UNDER FIRE IS COMMUNICATIONS MINISTER CHANG PO-CHUN. 

IN AUGUST THE AGENCY QUOTED LO AS CONFESSING HE WAS TOO FAR TO 
THE RIGHT. TODAY IT SAID LO "WAS WARNED HE WOULD WIN GREATER 


LENIENCY FROM THE PEOPLE IF HE CONFESSES HONESTLY."

TOKYO, DEC. 26 (AP)-RED CHINA IS HAVING TROUBLE WITH AGITATION 
POR AW TROEPENDENT-REPUBCTC BY NOMAD TRIBES IN THE WILD PROVINCE OF 
* 

RADIO PEIPING SAID TODAY "REACTIONARY MINORITY RACIAL ELEMENTS® IN 

NORTHERN SINKIANG ARE AGITATING FOR AN INDEPENDENT EAST TURKISTAN 
6 

SINKIANG IS A RUGGED 700,000 SQUARE MILES OF DESERT AND MOUNTAINS 
TOUCHING THE SOVIET UNION ON THE WEST AND NORTH. CHINESE 
COLONISTS MAKE UP ONLY ABOUT EIGHT PER CENT OF THE ESTIMATED FOUR 
MILLION POPULATION. 

ABOUT 80 PER CENT OF THE PEOPLE ARE TURKIC UIGURS AND THE NORTHERN 
PART OF THE PROVINCE HAS BEEN ORGANIZED UNDER THE COMMUNISTS AS THE 
UIGUR AUTONOMOUS REGION. KAZAKHS MAKE UP ABOUT 8 PER CENT OF THE 
POPULATION AND KIRGIZ AND MONGOLS SPLIT THE REST. THE PROVINCE IS 75 
PER CENT MOSLEM, 

RADIO PEIPING QUOTED THE LOCAL COMMUNIST BOSS, SAI FU-TIN, AS 
SAYING "REGIONAL RACIALISTS® ARE OPPOSING A CHANGE TO A SOCIALIST 
(COMMUNIST) SOCIETY, WANT TO OVERTHROW THE COMMUNIST GOVERNMENT AND 
ARE TRYING TO EXPEL THE CHINESE. AGITATION HAS INCREASED SINCE LAST 
YEAR, SAI REPORTED. 

THE RELATED PEOPLE ON BOTH SIDES OF THE SOVIET BORDER HAVE ALWAYS 
REGARDED CHINESE AND RUSSIANS AS FOREIGN IMPERIALISTS. FOLLOWING 
THE BOLSHEVIK REVOLUTION IN RUSSIA, THE COMMUNISTS PUT DOWN AFTER 
SEVERAL YEARS OF SPORADIC FIGHTING A STRONG MOVEMENT IN SOVIET CENTRAL 
ASIA FOR A TURKISTAN REPUBLIC. 

THE BROADCAST HEARD HERE SAID A REPORT ON UNREST WAS MADE DEC. 16 
BY SAI, WHO IS CHIEF OF THE UIGURSTAN AUTONOMOUS REGION AND SECRETARY 
OF THE REGIONAL COMMUNIST PARTY COMMITTEE. HIS REPORT WAS TO A 
CONFERENCE TO DEBATE THE PROBLEMS OF REGIONAL RACIALIST IDEOLOGY 
AMONG MINORITY GROUPS AND THE INDEPENDENCE STRUGGLE. 

SAI SAID THERE ARE NOW 50,000 PARTY MEMBERS AND 108,000 
COMMUNIST YOUTHS AMONG MINORITY RACES IN THE UIGUR REGION. THIS 
FIGURE WOULD BE HIGHER THAN.PARTY MEMBERSHIP IN THE REST OF CHINA.

MISSILE MONEY 
BY ELTON C. FAY 


WASHINGTON, DEC. 27 (AP)-THE UNITED STATES HAS PUT MORE THAN 17 
BILLION DOLLARS “INTO-RESEAREME DEVELOPMENT AND PRODUCTION OF MISSILES 
OF VARIOUS TYPES SINCE IT BEGAN EXPLORING THE FEASIBILITY OF THOSE 
WEAPONS IN WORLD WAR II DAYS. 

ALL BUT ABOUT A HALF BILLION DOLLARS OF THE TOTAL HAS BEEN PRO- 
CRAMMED SINCE THE BEGINNING OF THE KOREAN WAR IN 1950 SET OFF THE 
REARMAMENT PROGRAM. 

CONGRESSIONAL COMMITTEES ARE INVESTIGATING OR PREPARING TO INVESTI- 
CATE THE WHOLE MISSILE PROBLEM, INCLUDING THE QUESTIONS OF THE PAST, 
PRESENT AND FUTURE ADEQUACY OF FUNDS, AND WHETHER THE PENTAGON HAS 
PEFEN DILIGENT IN SPENDING THE MONEY PROVIDED BY CONGRESS. 

FICURES MADE AVAILABLE AT THE PENTAGON TODAY SHOW THAT $17,178,- 
000.000 (B) HAS BEEN ASSIGNED TO MISSILE PROGRAMS SINCE *FISCAL 
YFAR 194€ AND PRIOR." THE FIGURE INCLUDES AN ESTIMATED $4,638 ,000,000 
FOR THE CURRENT FISCAL YEAR, BUT DOFS NOT TAKE INTO ACCOUNT AN 
EXTRA BILLION DOLLARS WHICH SECRETARY OF DEFENSE MCELROY HAS SAID HE 
WILL ASK FROM CONGRESS. 

THE TOTAL COVERS OBLIGATIONS TO WHICH THE MILITARY SERVICES 
COMMITTED THEMSELVES IN THE WHOLE BROAD MISSILE FIELD. 

A’ DEFENSE DEPARTMENT SUMMARY SAID IT INCLUDES "THE COST OF BRINGING 
CUIDED MISSILE WEAPON SYSTEMS TO AN OPERATIONAL STATUS, RESEARCH AND 
DEVELOPMENT, PRODUCTION FACILITY EXPANSION AND TOOLING, PROCUREMENT y 
CONTRACT ANB MILITARY OVERHEAD TO SUPPORT MISSILE TESTING AND CERTAIN 
CONSTRUCTION COSTS FOR RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT.® 

IT DOES NOT INCLUDE SUCH ITEMS AS THE COST OF RUNNING OPERATIONAL 
SITES. LIKE THOSE FOR THE NIKE ANTIAIRCRAFT MISSILE. 

ALTHOUGH THE TABULATION REFERS TO "GUIDED MISSILES" THE DEFINITION 
INCLUDES BALLISTIC MISSILES--THE INTERMEDIATE AND INTERCONTINENTAL 
RANGE WEAPONS UPON WHICH THE PRIME ATTENTION OF CONGRESSIONAL COM- 
MITTFES 1S FOCUSED. 

FROM THE TIME THE SERVICES BEGAN ANALYZING CAPTURED GERMAN MISSILES 
LATE IN WORLD WAR II AND STUDYING DEVELOPMENT OF THEIR OWN WEAPONS 
THROUGH JUNE 30, 1946, THE TOTAL MISSILE PROGRAM AMOUNTED TO ABOUT 
70 MILLION DOLLARS. DURING THE 1947 FISCAL YEAR ENDING JUNE 30,

SHREVEPORT, LAs, DEC. 27 (AP)-BENNIE BENDER, LOCAL DEVELOPER, SAID 

HE FRENCH GOVERNMENT TO CONSTRUCT AN 
80 MILLION DOLLAR PIPELINE FROM THE MEDITERRANEAN SEA TO FIELDS DEEP 
IN THE SAHARA DESERT. 

THE PROJECT CAME TO LIGHT WHEN BENDER REGISTERED THE NAME AFRIQUE 
DU NORD DEVELOPMENT SOCIETE WITH THE CLERK OF COURT HERE. THE 
REGISTRATION PAPERS DESCRIBED THE PURPOSE OF THE FIRM AS ERECTION OF 
AN 18-INCH PIPELINE IN ALGERIA AND LIBYA. 

COR ENDER HAS BEEN IN THE PIPELINE BUSINESS IN THIS COUNTRY AND ABROAD 

HE TOLD A REPORTER "NEGOTIATIONS WITH THE FRENCH GOVERNMENT AND 
WITH THE KING AND PREMIER OF LIBYA HAVE BEEN UNDERWAY FOR SOME MONTHS.® 

®I AM DUE BACK IN PARIS JAN. 5 AND HOPE THAT ALL DETAILS WILL BE 
WORKED OUT AND A CONTRACT SIGNED BY JAN. 6." 

THE PROPOSED PIPELINE, HE SAID, WOULD BE 850 MILES LONG AND WOULD 
BRING PRODUCTS FROM THE NEWLY DISCOVERED HASSAI-MESSAOUD FIELD IN 
ALGERIA TO A MEDITERRANEAN SEAPORT. 

BENDER SAID THE DESERT OIL FIELD PRODUCES FROM SOME 500 TO 600 
FEET OF PAY SAND AT 11,500 FEETe HE DESCRIBED IT AS THE RICHEST OIL 
FIND TO DATE IN THE ARAB WORLD. 

EXPLORATION AND DRILLING, HE SAID, WAS DONE BY THE FRENCH GOVERN- 
MENT AND PRIVATE FRENCH INVESTORS. HE SAID COST OF EACH WELL WAS 
WELL OVER A MILLION DOLLARS, LARGELY BECAUSE OF EXPENSE OF TRANSPORTING 
MATERIALS ACROSS THE DESERT. 

THE SITUATION, BENDER SAID, IS THAT THE FRENCH GOVERNMENT HAS A HUGE 
OIL DISCOVERY, ONE BIC ENOUGH TO STABILIZE THE ECONOMY OF THE ENTIRE 
NATION, BUT WO WAY TO TRANSPORT THE OIL TO THE SEAs 

BENDER HAS ONE PARTNER IN THE PIPELINE VENTURE, He Le (BUCK) 

REMMEL OF LITTLE ROCK, ARKe, WHOSE FATHER ORGANIZED THE BANKER ’S 
TRUST CO. OF LITTLE ROCK. RE SAID HE WOULD TAKE OTHER PARTNERS IF 
THE CONTRACT WITH THE FRENCH GOVERNMENT GOES THROUGH.

A SPOKESMAN SAID THAT SINCE 1948, WHEN THE ARMED SERVICES FIRST 
ADOPTED GENERAL PROGRAMS FOR ELIMINATING FROM THEIR ROLLS MEN CONSIDERE 
SECURITY RISKS, THE AIR FORCE HAS CONSIDERED 4,236 CASES IN WHICH 
SECURITY ISSUES WERE RAISED. 

OF THESE, 168 OFFICERS AND ENLISTED MEN WERE DISCHARGED FOR 
SECURITY REASONS, BUT 68 WERE GIVEN HONORABLE DISCHARGES AND 90 GENERAL 
DISCHARGES (UNDER HONORABLE CONDITIONS). 

THE SPOKESMAN SAID THE GENERAL AIR FORCE POLICY, WHEN DISCHARGING 
A MAN AS A SECURITY RISK, WAS TO GIVE HIM AN HONORABLE DISCHARGE 
OR ONE UNDER HONORABLE CONDITIONS IF THE ACTIVITIES WHICH CAUSED HIM 
TO BE CONSIDERED A RISK HAD TAKEN PLACE BEFORE HIS MILITARY SERVICE 
AND HIS SERVICE RECORD WAS GOOD. 

THE ARMY THURSDAY DISCLOSED THAT A REVIEW OF ALL ITS SECURITY RISK 
DISCHARGES BETWEEN 1948 AND 1955 SO FAR KAS COVERED 650 OF THE 726 
DISCHARGES AND THAT IN ABOUT TWO OUT OF FIVE CASES A HIGHER 
GRADE DISCHARGE HAS BEEN SUBSTITUTED THE ORIGINAL ONE. 

THE AIR FORCE SPOKESMAN SAID THE A ORCE HAD NOT UNDERTAKEN 
ANY GENERAL REVIEW OF THE 10 UNDES DISCHARGES IT ISSUED AND THAT 
SO FAR AS HE KNEW THERE HAD BEEN ,*REQUEST FOR REVIEW OF ANY OF THESE 
ON AN INDIVIDUAL BASIS. :

- ~ DEFENSE DEPARTMENT WAS REPORTED TODAY 
TO G IATE START ON BUILDING THE FIRST THREE 
NUCLEAR POWERED SUBMARINES SPECIALLY DESIGNED FOR FIRING THE NAVY'S 
POLARIS INTERMEDIATE RANGE BALLISTIC MISSILE (IRBM). 

FUNDS FOR PROCURING MATERIAL AND CARRYING FORWARD THE DESIGN OF THE 
BOATS WOULD BE INCLUDEP IN THE PROPOSED ONE BILLION DOLLAR SUPPLEMENTAL 
MILITARY BUDGET FOR THE CURRENT FISCAL YEAR, WHICH ENDS NEXT JUNE 30. 

THIS WOULD REPRESENT A SPEED-UP OF THE ORIGINAL INTENTION TO INCLUDE 
POLARIS SUBMARINE MONEY IN THE NEXT FISCAL YEAR'S BUDGET. THE NAVY HAD 
SAID IT EXPECTED TO ASK FUNDS IN THAT BUDGET FOR A START ON ONE SUCH 
SUBMARINE. CONGRESSIONAL ACTION ON FUTURE BUDGETS USUALLY IS NOT COM 
PLETED UNTIL MID-SUMMER. 

SECRETARY OF DEFENSE MCELROY TOLD NEWSMEN LAST WEEK HE WOULD SUBMIT 
A REQUEST FOR APPROXIMATELY ONE BILLION DOLLARS OF ADDITIONAL FUNDS FOR 
THE 1958 FISCAL YEAR. HE SAID A LARGE PART OF THIS WOULD GO INTO 
MISSILE PROGRAMS, 

IN ADDITION, IT IS EXPECTED THE SUPPLEMENTAL MONEY BILL WILL INCLUDE 
REQUESTS FOR FUNDS TO BE USED IN RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT AND FOR EX- 
PANDING THE PROGRAM OF DISPERSING STRATEGIC AIR COMMAND (SAC) BASES. 

ALL THREE PROJECTS WERE INCLUDED IN TOPICS SINGLED OUT BY PRESIDENT 
EISENHOWER IN HIS FIRST NATIONWIDE ADDRESS ON DEFENSE NEEDS LAST MONTH. 

PACING THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE POLARIS MISSILE ITSELF HAS BEEN A 
SPECIAL TASK FORCE OF SHIP DESIGNERS AND ARMAMENT EXPERTS ENGAGED IN 
DEVELOPING A FINAL DESIGN FOR A POLARIS-FIRING SUBMERSIBLE. NAVY OF- 
FICIALS HAVE SAID THAT "SEVERAL DIFFERENT SUBMARINE DESIGNS" HAVE BEEN 
UNDER CONSIDERATION. 

BECAUSE OF REQUIREMENTS FOR HANDLING THE POLARIS MISSILE, THE INTER- 
IOR LAYOUT OF THE NEW SUBMARINES PRESUMABLY WILL BE CHANGED SUBSTANTI- 
ALLY FROM THAT OF EVEN THE NEWEST DESIGN NUCLEAR SUBMARINE FITTED FOR 
CONVENTIONAL TORPEDO FIRING, MINE LAYING OR GUIDED MISSILE LAUNCHING. 

UNLIKE THE SURFACE-LAUNCHED REGULUS GUIDED MISSILE, THE POLARIS

THE FIRST STAGE OF THE ROCKET ENGINE SYSTEM HAS BEEN TEST FIRED. AT 
CAPE CANAVERAL, FLAe, THE NAVY HAS BEGUN WORK ON BUILDING A SIMULATED 
SUBMARINE LAUNCHING PLATFORM EQUIPPED SO THAT THE ROLL AND PITCH OF A 
VESSEL AT SEA CAN BE DUPLICATED IN TEST FIRINGS OF THE POLARIS. IN AD- 
DITION, A PORT FACILITY AT THE CAPE CANAVERAL SITE IS UNDERSTOOD TO BE 
UNDERGOING ALTERATIONS TO PERMIT THE MOORING OF SUBMARINES AND OTHER 
COMBATANT TYPE SURFACE SHIPS WITHIN THE TEST SITE. 


IN ANOTHER FIELD OF BUDGET MAKING, THE NAVY HAS LEARNED FROM THE DE- 
FENSE DEPARTMENT THAT IT MUST PUT OVER FOR A YEAR ITS PLAN TO START 


CONSTRUCTION OF THE HULL OF A SECOND NUCLEAR POWERED AIRCRAFT CARRIER. 
THE DEPARTMENT WAS REPORTED TODAY TO HAVE TURNED DOWN THE NAVY'S RE- 
QUEST FOR INCLUSION OF SUCH MONEY IN THE COMING YEAR'S eg ALTHOUGH 


THE DEPARTMENT HAS APPROVED A FUND REQUEST TO BEGIN DESIGN AND CONSTRUC- 
TION OF REACTORS FOR THE SECOND 80,000-TON FLATTOP. 

FUNDS FOR STARTING WORK ON THE FIRST CARRIER WERE PROVIDED IN THE 
CURRENT BUDGET. THE DEFENSE DEPARTMENT'S REPORTED REFUSAL TO INCLUDE 
MONEY FOR THE HULL OF THE SECOND CARRIER IN THE NEXT REGULAR BUDGET 
mn, THE NAVY'S CHERISHED ONE-A-YEAR CARRIER PROGRAM WOULD BE IN- 

ONE FACTOR UNDERSTOOD TO HAVE RANKED HIGH AMONG THE REASONS FOR THE 
DEFENSE DEPARTMENT'S TURN-DOWN OF THE CARRIER REQUEST IS A DESIRE TO 
BUILD UP THE NUCLEAR SUBMARINE FORCE QUICKLY. 

THE AIR FORCE*S LONG RANGE PROGRAM TO IMPROVE THE SAC DISPERSAL 
SITUATION ENCOUNTERED ECONOMY CUTBACKS. ONE OF THE FIRST RESULTS OF THE 
ORIGINAL DECISION TO CURTAIL MILITARY SPENDING WAS TO TERMINATE A NUMBER 
OF AIR BASE BUILDING PLANS. 


THE REPORTED INCLUSION IN THE SUPPLEMENTAL BUDGET REQUEST OF MONEY 
FOR SAC DISPERSAL APPARENTLY REVERSES THAT POLICY. 

PURPOSE OF THE PROGRAM IS TO SPREAD OUT THE NUMBER OF SAC LONG RANGE 
AND MEDIUM BOMBERS SPOTTED ON ANY ONE BASE AT ANY ONE TIME--WHERE THEY 
COULD BE DESTROYED BY A SUDDEN AIR STRIKE. 

AIR FORCE OFFICIALS SAY THAT THE DISPERSAL PROGRAM DOES NOT _ MEAN 
THAT ELABORATE, COMPLETE BASES WILL HAVE TO BE CONSTRUCTED. INSTEAD, 
THEY MAY MORE NEARLY RESEMBLE FORWARD “STAGING® BASES, WITH ONLY THE 
ESSENTIALS FOR FUELING, ARMING AND MAINTENANCE, AND BUILT AROUND A 
SINGLE LONG RUNWAY AND A PARKING STAND AREA.

THIS, SAID INFORMED SOURCES, WAS BECAUSE THE TIME NEEDED FOR PERFECT- 
ING AND CONSTRUCTING A NEW MULTIPLE REACTOR POWER PLANT WOULD BE LONGER 
THAN THAT NEEDED FOR BUILDING THE SHIP ITSELF. MOREOVER, PROGRESS OF

THE SECOND SHIP. 

THE NAVY, SINCE BUILDING THE FIRST, CONVENTIONALLY POWERED FORRESTAL 
CLASS CARRIER--A 60,000-TON SHIP--HAD PLANNED TO BUILD ONE BIG CARRIER A 
YEAR FOR AT LEAST 16 YEARS. WHEN THE DESIGN FOR THE BIGGER, 80,000-TON 
NUCLEAR POWERED CARRIER WAS READY, THE NAVY SHIFTED THE GOAL FROM CON- 
VENTIONAL TO ATOM-DRIVEN CARRIERS. THE REPORTED DECISION OF THE DE- 
FENSE DEPARTMENT TO LEAVE OUT THE CARRIER HULL FUNDS FROM THE FISCAL 
1959 BUDGET WOULD INTERRUPT THE NAVY PROGRAM'S CONTINUITY. 

ONE FACTOR POSSIBLY INFLUENCING THE ACTION WAS A DECISION TO PRESS 
FORWARD WITH THE NUCLEAR SUBMARINE PROGRAM, APPLYING FUNDS WHICH WOULD 
HAVE GONE TO THE CARRIER HULL TO EXPEDITING SUBMARINE CONSTRUCTION. 

COST OF THE FIRST ATOMIC CARRIER HAS BEEN ESTIMATED AS HIGH AS 318 
MILLION DOLLARS. THIS FIGURE INCLUDES THE COST OF HULL AND THE REACT-

MODERN CARRIER.

GOT FROM CONGRESS.»

~-SOVIET UNION-- 


BY HAROLD K.MILKS 

(ADVANCE) MOSCOW. DECe28 (AP)-THE SOVIET UNION WILL ENTER THE 
NEW YEAR WITH ITS COLD WAR OPPONENTS ON THE DEFENSIVE IN SEVERAL 

SOVIET SCIENTIFIC AND ENGINEERING ACHIEVEMENTS IN LAUNCHING THE 
FIRST EARTH SATELLITES AND THE INTERCONTINENTAL BALLISTIC MISSILE 
BACKED BY THE APPARENT POLITICAL UNITY OF THE COMMUNIST WORLD, MAKE 
1958 LOOK LIKE A TOUGH YEAR FOR THE WEST. 

IT IS CERTAIN THE KREMLIN LEADERS HEADED BY NIKITA KHRUSHCHEV 
WILL PUSH THEIR SCIENTISTS TO MAINTAIN THEIR LEAD AS THE BASIS OF A 
MAJOR PROPAGANDA CAMPAIGN TO WIN THE WORLD FOR COMMUNISM. 

MORE EMPHASIS WILL BE PLACED ON ROCKETS AND MISSILES IN THE 
COMING YEAR. AT THE SAME TIME INCREASING PRODUCTION OF FOODSTUFFS 
AND NEW RECORDS OF INDUSTRIAL OUTPUT ENABLE SOVIET LEADERS TO HOLD 
OUT THE PROMISE OF A BETTER STANDARD OF LIVING FOR THEIR PEOPLES. 

POLITICALLY, THE KREMLIN HAS EMERGED FROM A SERIES OF MIDDLE EAST 
CRISES AS THE SEEMING FRIEND OF ARAB NATIONALISTS AND THE PROTECTOR 
OF THE EGYPTIAN-SYRIAN BLOC. IT HAS LOST NO FRIENDS IN THE 
SO-CALLED NEUTRAL BLOC. THE HUNGARIAN REVOLT, POSING THE QUESTION 
OF SATELLITE UNREST. HAS FADED INTO THE BACKGROUND. 

FOR THE FIRST TIME, COMMUNIST LEADERS FEEL THEY ARE ABLE TO 
BARGAIN WITHIN OR WITHOUT THE UNITED NATIONS FROM A POSITION OF 
POLITICAL, SCIENTIFIC AND MILITARY STRENGTH.

SUBJECT TO CENSORSHIP. 3

WORLD PEACE TO PREVAIL IN ;

THE STRAIN. 

THE PEOPLES OF MUCH OF WESTERN EUROPE ARE LIVING BETTER THAN EVER

--EASTERN EUROPE-- a | 
BY RICHARD KASISCHKE 

VIENNA, DEC.28 (AP)-THE CHANCES OF MORE FREEDOM FOR RUSSIA'S EAST 
EUROPEAN SATELLITES IN 1958 ARE JUST ABOUT NILe 

MOSCOW'S HOLD OVER EASTERN EUROPE, SORELY STRAINED BY THE 1956 
UPHEAVALS IN POLAND AND HUNGARY, HAS BEEN TIGHTENED. NIKITA 
KHRUSHCHEV, VICTORIOUS OVER KREMLIN RIVALS FOR PARTY POWER AND 
BASKING IN THE GLOW OF SOVIET BABY MOONS, NOW MAY MAKE THINGS EVEN 
HARDER FOR THE SATELLITE PEOPLES. 

HUNGARY AGAIN IS IN SUBJUGATION TO A MOSCOW PUPPET REGIMES IT Is_ 
STILL ARRESTING AND PUTTING TO DEATH LEADERS OF THE REBELLION CRUSHED 
BY SOVIET TROOPS MORE THAN A YEAR AGO. NINE RUSSIAN DIVISIONS STILL 
STAND GUARD, AND THE HUNGARIAN PEOPLE SEEM LIKELY TO HAVE TO ENDURE 
YET ANOTHER YEAR OF DESPAIR. 

IN POLAND, NEITHER FREE NOR IN SUBJUGATION, THE LIBERTIES WON IN 
1956 ARE EVAPORATING SLOWLY. 

POLISH COMMUNISM WILL BE PREOCCUPIED WITH A MASSIVE, BLOODLESS 
PURGE OF ITS MEMBERSHIP ROLLS. THEN IT MAY HOLD A LONG-DELAYED PARTY 
CONGRESS TO FORGE NEW POLICIES THAT PROBABLY WILL BOIL DOWN TO 
ANOTHER PRODUCTION DRIVE. LABOR TROUBLES ARE LIKELY UNLESS THE 
GOVERNMENT CAN LIFT ITS WAGE FREEZE. 

CZECHOSLOVAKIA, QUIETEST AND MOST PROSPEROUS OF THE SATELLITES 
HAS HAD A RASH OF ARRESTS OF ALLEGED SPIES AND PRO-WESTERN ELEMENTS. 
THE REGIME HAS WARNED IT WILL TOLERATE NO FREEDOM NOTIONS. 

ROMANIA, RULED QUIETLY BY A SMOOTH MACHINE, STILL HAS FELT IT 
NECESSARY to TIGHTEN PENAL CODES AND SHARPEN PENALTIES FOR TRIVIAL 
0 : 


CONLIOF IM anQOVFe: 7° 


BULGARIA, RIDDEN BY UN CULTIES, IS 
wscou"s IAy Y UNEMPLOYMENT AND ECONOMIC DIFFI : a 
LAVIA'S MARSHAL TITO WILL CONTINUE TO BALANCE OFF EA 
WEST IN AN EFFORT TO ESCAPE RUSSIA'S BEAR HUG. HE WILL TRY TO AVOID 
ANY OPEN DISPUTES WITH THE COMMUNIST FAMILY, BUT MAY SEEK A WAY OF 

LEADING THE UNITED STATES TO HAVE MORE CONFIDENCE IN HIM. NEW 
CREDITS AND LOANS WILL BE NEEDED IN THE FIVE YEARS AHEAD. 

AUSTRIA, THE LITTLE INDEPENDENT NATION ALMOST SURROUNDED BY A 
COMMUNIST SEA, IS PROSPEROUS AND STABLE. 
--MIDDLE EKAST--

IN ADDITION THE UNITED STATES HAS WHAT IT CALLS ®CONTINUING POLITICAL
