A WARNING THAT CLOSER FREE WORLD LIAISON IS AN IMPERATIVE NEED WAS 
SOUNDED AUG. 26, WHEN RUSSIA LAUNCHED THE WORLD'S FIRST INTERCONTINENTAL 
BALLISTIC MISSILE. IT WAS DRAMATICALLY SOUNDED AGAIN OCT. 4 WHEN RUSSIA 
SENT THE WORLD’S FIRST MAN-MADE EARTH SATELLITE INTO ORBIT. 

THAT MEANT ONE THING: A BIG SURGE IN RUSSIA'S LONG-RANGE OFFENSIVE 
POWER. TO HELP MEET IT, THE ALLIANCES HAD TO BE PULLED CLOSER TOGETHER. 

PRESIDENT EISENHOWER AND BRITISH PRIME MINISTER HAROLD MACMILLAN MET 
IN WASHINGTON IN LATE OCTOBER. THEY ISSUED WHAT CAME TO BE KNOWN AS 
"THE DECLARATION OF INTERDEPENDENCE." IT CALLED FOR GREATER FREE WORLD 
COOPERATION AND SHARING OF RESPONSIBILITY. 

THE NATO HEADS OF GOVERNMENT FOLLOWED THIS UP AT PARIS THIS MONTH. 
THEY ENDORSED GREATER INTERDEPENDENCE AND INTERLOCKING OF ALLIANCES 
WHILE TAKING A BASIC DECISION TO TRY TO NEGOTIATE WITH RUSSIA AND AT 
THE SAME TIME SEE ABOUT SETTING UP INTERMEDIATE RANGE BALLISTIC MISSILE 
BASES IN WEST EUROPE, 

NATO IS THE MOST IMPORTANT AMONG THE NINE DEFENSE AGREEMENTS IN 
WHICH THE UNITED STATES IS INVOLVED. 

PRESIDENT EISENHOWER TOLD CONGRESS LAST YEAR, IN HIS DEFENSE MESSAGE, 
THAT AMERICA'S ALLIES HAVE RAISED 200 DIVISIONS AROUND THE GLOBE. IN 
ADDITION, HE SAID, THE ALLIES HAD 27,000 AIRCRAFT AND 2,500 COMBAT

IN NATO), IRAQ AND IRAN.

AFRICAN-ASIAN BUDGET (35790) 

BY ANTOINE YARED 

CAIRO, DEC. 29 CAP)-NATIONALIZATION RANKED HIGH AMONG TOPICS IN THE 
DRAFTING OF RESOLUTIONS AT THE AFRICAN-ASIAN CONFERENCE TONIGHT. 

AN INFORMED SOURCE SAIN A RESOLUTION COMPLETED IN THE ECONOMIC 
COMMITTEE APPROVES GOVERNMENT TAKEOVER OF PROPERTY AS "LAWFUL MEANS 


AND A RIGHT WHICH IS ACKNOWLEDGED FOR EVERY NATION IN ACCORDANCE 
WITH THE PRINCIPLES OF NATIONAL SOVEREIGNTY.®* 

THE COMMITTEE WAS REPORTED READY TO ADOPT IT. 

THE RESOLUTION WOULD STILL BE SUBJECT TO APPROVAL BY THE FULL 
CONFERENCE OF 400 DELEGATES FROM 42 NATIONS AND COLONIES AT ITS CLOSING 
BUSINESS SESSION WEDNESDAY. 

FIRST MENTION OF NATIONALIZATION AT THE CONFERENCE WAS MADE 
FRIDAY IN THE ECONOMIC REPORT BY THE SOVIET DELEGATION. 

THE RUSSIANS OFFERED TO EXTEND ECONOMIC AID OR LOANS FOR ALL 
AFRICAN-ASIAN COUNTRIES. BUT THEIR REPORT ALSO IN EFFECT CALLED FOR 
NATIONALIZATION OF FOREIGN ENTERPRISES AS STEPS TOWARD OBTAINING 
FUNDS FOR INDUSTRIAL DEVELOPMENT. 

THE REPORT PRAISED EGYPT FOR NATIONALIZING THE SUEZ CANAL AND ALSO 
THE "INDONESIAN PATRIOTS NOW FIGHTING TO NATIONALIZE DUTCH BANKS AND 
OTHER ENTERPRISES.* 

ALL CONFERENCE COMMITTEES AND SUBCOMMITTEES SAT DOWN TONIGHT TQ, 

PUT THE FINAL TOUCHES ON RESOLUTIONS AFTER A DAY-LONG OUTING AT 1957 
EGYPT'S LARGEST TEXTILE PLANT, 60 MILES NORTH OF CAIRO. 

IT APPEARED THERE WILL BE NO MENTION OF AN AFRICAN-ASIAN COMMON 
MARKET IN ANY ECONOMIC COMMITTEE RESOLUTIONS. INSTEAD A DRAFT 
RESOLUTION REPORTEDLY CALLS FOR STUDY AND EXPLORATION OF *®ALL CONCRETE

TO REFUSE.

FLEET SAID TOBAY ATOMIC DEPTH CHARGES AND GENERALLY IMPROVED DEFENSES 
WOULD MAKE A RUSSIAN SUBMARINE ATTACK AGAINST AMERICAN SHORES "AN UN- 
POPULAR MOVE" FOR THE ATTACKERS. 

ADM. JERAULD WRICHT. AFTER MENTIONING NEW MEASURES TAKEN TO PREVENT 
SUBMARINE ATTACKS. CALLED FOR MORE MONEY, RESEARCH, SHIPS AND AIRCRAFT 
TO BOLSTER DEFENSES AGAINST MISSILE-LAUNCHING UNDERSEAS CRAFT. 

HE TOLD A PENTAGON NEWS CONFERENCE THAT AMERICAN SCIENTISTS HAVE 
"CONE ABOUT AS FAR AS THEY CAN WITH THE MONEY AVAILABLE® IN PERFECTING 
MEANS TO DETECT AND DESTROY SUBMARINESe AS THE OFFICER WITH IMMEDIATE 
RESPONSIBILITY FOR THE DEFENSE OF THE ATLANTIC SEABOARD, HE ADDED, HE 
HAD ASKED FOR "SUBSTANTIALLY MORE FORCES THAN WE NOW HAVE." 

WRIGHT SAID RUSSIAN SUBMARINES HAVE BEEN SPOTTED THROUGHOUT THE 
ATLANTIC OCEAN, BUT THAT THE SIGHTINGS HAD CONVEYED NO PARTICULAR 
OFFENSIVE PATTERN. .

WRIGHT VOICED GREAT HOPES FOR THE NAVY'S POLARIS (CAP P) INTERMEDIATE

NEXT YEAR OR TWO." HE SAID THE POLARIS AND SUBMARINES DESIGNED TO 
FIRE THEM SHOULD BECOME OPERATIONAL ABOUT THE SAME TIME AND THAT WHEN 
THEY WERE READY THEY COULD BE USED TO SUPPORT THE NATO DEFENSES IN WEST- 
ERN EUROPE. 

IN ADDITION TO HIS AMERICAN COMMAND, WRIGHT HOLDS THE NATO POST OF 
SUPREME ALLIED COMMANDER ATLANTIC. 

THE ADMIRAL SAID THE NAVY'S NEW ATOMIC DEPTH CHARGE, NAMED "BETTY 
HAD GREATLY EXTENDED THE KILLING RANGE OF ANTI-SUBMARINE WEAPONS, BUT 
THAT ITS USE REQUIRED THE HIGHEST COORDINATION BETWEEN THE LAUNCHING 
AIRCRAFT AND SUPPORTING SURFACE SHIPS. 

THE NAVY IS ALSO DEVELOPING A NUCLEAR DEPTH CHARGE TO BE LAUNCHED 
FROM SURFACE SHIPS. IT IS CALLED "LULU." WRIGHT DID NOT SAY WHEN 
THIS ADDITIONAL WEAPON WILL BE READY FOR USE.

NUCLEAR PLANE (320) 

BY EDMOND LE BRETON 
WASHINGTON, DEC. 

PENTAGON TO REC 


50 (AP) - INFORMED OFFICIALS SAID TODAY THEY EXPECT TH 
OMMEND TO PRESIDENT EISENHOWER A COMPROMISE THAT COULD 
CLEAR THE WAY FOR BUILDING AN ATOM-DRIVEN AIRPLANE. 


FOR YEARS THE NUCLEAR PLANE PROGRAM 


DESPITE PRODDING FROM CONGRESS 
HAS BEEN KEPT ON A BARE SUBSISTENCE BASIS AND PERENIALLY THREATENED WI 
COMPLETE SHUTDOWN. 


ONE REASON WHY NO FUNDS HAVE BEEN PROVIDED FOR ACTUALLY BUILDING 
AN AIRCRAFT HAS BEEN A CONTINUING ARGUMENT AS TO WHETHER THE UNITED 
STATES SHOULD PRESS TO GET AN A-PLANE INTO THE AIR -- EVEN IF IT 
OBVIOUSLY WAS TOO PRIMITIVE TO HAVE ANY MILITARY WORTH -- OR TAKE MORE 
TIME AND PRODUCE AN ACTUAL FORERUNNER TO OPERATIONAL MILITARY PLANES. 

THE REPORTED COMPROMISE WOULD CALL FOR BUILDING A PLANE WHICH IS 
NEITHER PRIMITIVE NOR A FINISHED PRODUCT. IT MIGHT, AS PROPONENTS HAVE 
URGED, USE THE AIRFRAME OF AN EXISTING CONVENTIONAL PLANE ADAPTED FOR A 
NUCLEAR ENGINE. BUT ENOUGH RESEARCH WOULD BE INCORPORATED INTO IT So

OF IE OPERATIONAL PLANS FOR BOTH LONG-RANGE, AIR-BREATHING GUIDED 
MISSILES AND INTERMEDIATE RANGE BALLISTIC MISSILES ARE UNDERSTOOD TO 
HAVE BEEN COMPLETED AND INCORPORATED IN THE OVER-ALL WARTIME PLANS OF

THE AIR FORCE MAINTAINS THREE BASIC STRATEGIC BLUEPRINTS WHICH

YEARS« THEY ARE THE SHORT RANGE ®WARTIME CAPABILITIES PLAN"; THE

FUTURE; AND THE "LONG RANGE WARTIME OBJECTIVES PLANe™ AN AIR FORCE

IONS AND VULNERABILITIES."

DOWN IN THE EARTH'S ATMOSPHERE.

MAXIMUM ACCURATE RANGE OF 1.500 MILES -- TO BE MADE LATE IN 1958.

CHICAGO, DEC. 30 (AP)-ELECTRICITY PRODUCED FROM ATOMIC ENERGY: HAS 
MOVED ANOTHER STEP CLOSER TO COMPETITIVE COSTS, THE ARGONNE NATIONAL 
LABORATORY REPORTED TODAY. 

_..BY INCREASING THE POWER OUTPUT OF THE LAB'S EXPERIMENTAL BOILING 
WATER REACTOR FROM 20,000 TO 50,000 KILOWATTS OF HEAT, THE COST WAS 
CUT FROM 52 MILLS TO 32 PER KILOWATT HOUR--THE CHEAPEST ATOMIC- 
PRODUCED ELECTRICITY IN THE UNITED STATES. 
_ BROKEN DOWN INTO DOLLARS AND CENTS, ARGONNE OFFICIALS SAID THE COST 
WAS REDUCED FROM 5.2 CENTS PER KILOWATT HOUR TO 302 CENTS. 

A CHICAGO HOME, FOR EXAMPLE, USES 8 KILOWATT HOURS A DAY WHICH WOULD 
PUT THE COST OF NUCLEAR-PRODUCED ELECTRICITY AT ABOUT 25 CENTS A DAY-- 
STILL FOUR TIMES HIGHER THAN THE COST OF CONVENTIONALLY PRODUCED 


ELECTRICITY~ 

"ECONOMIC NUCLEAR POWER IN THE UNITED STATES STILL SEEMS RELATIVELY 
FAR OFF," SAID DRe BERNARD SPINRAD, DIRECTOR OF REACTOR ENGINEERING 
AT THE LEMONT, ILL. LABORATORY. | | 

"HOWEVER 26 MILLS PER KILOWATT HOUR WOULD BE ECONOMICAL IN SOME 
AREAS AND WE ARE NEARING THAT FIGURE. 

JOSEPH Me HARRER, THE REACTOR'S PROJECT MANAGER SAID "THE 32-MILL 
PER KILOWATT HOUR FIGURE PROBABLY CAN BE LOWERED WITHIN THE NEXT DECADE 
TO AROUND 10 MILLS PER KILOWATT HOUR." 

THE REACTOR PROVIDES MOST OF THE POWER USED AT ARGONNE’S 3,700 
ACRE SITE NEAR CHICAGO. |

HONOLULU. DEC 30 CAP)-ATTORNEY Ae Le WIRIN, HOLDING THE FIRST 
UNITED STATES CITIZEN'S PASSPORT FOR TRAVEL IN RED CHINA AND NORTH 
KOREA. SAID TODAY HE PLANS TO SPEND 90 DAYS GATHERING EVIDENCE IN THE 
TyO COMMUNIST COUNTRIES FOR A SEDITION TRIAL IN SAN FRANCISCO. 

WIRIN, A LOS ANGELES ATTORNEY FOR THE AMERICAN CIVIL LIBERTIES 
UNION, 12 DEFENDING JOHN W.ePOWELL AND HIS WIFE. THEY ARE ACCUSED OF 
SEDITION FOR ALLEGEDLY PRINTING FALSE STORIES IN THE CHINA MONTHLY 
REVIEW, WHICH THEY FORMERLY PUBLISHED IN SHANGHAI, THAT THE UNITED 
STATES ENGAGED IN GERM WARFARE IN KOREA. 

WIRIN HOLDS A LICENSE--ANOTHER FIRST--WHICH PERMITS HIM TO EXCHANGE 
UeSe DOLLARS FOR CHINESE COMMUNIST CURRENCY. 

HE ALSO HAS THE UNUSUAL DISTINCTION OF HAVING HIS ENTIRE TRIP PAID 
FOR BY THE UNITED STATES GOVERNMENT, INCLUDING HIS PLANE FARE, SEVEN 
CENTS A MILE TRAVEL PAY, AND $12 A DAY LIVING ALLOWANCE. 

THIS ALL CAME ABOUT AFTER FEDERAL DISTRICT JUDGE LOUIS E.GOODMAN IN 
SAN FRANCISCO WARNED THE GOVERNMENT THAT HE WOULD THROW THE POWELL 
CASE OUT OF COURT UNLESS WIRIN WAS PERMITTED TO OBTAIN DEFENSE INFOR- 
MATION HE SOUGHT IN CHINA.

CADVANCE)eeeNEW YORK, DEC. 31 (AP) -THE NEW YORK TIMES SAID 
TODAY THE UNITED STATES AND RUSSIA HAVE AGREED “IN PRINCIPLE® ON 
cae ate OF INFORMATION IN MANY AREAS OF SCIENCE, INDUSTRY, AND 
THE TIMES SAID IN A WASHINGTON DISPATCH THAT THE GENERAL 
AGREEMENT, WITH DETAILS NOT YET SPELLED OUT, HAS BEEN REACHED AS A 
RESULT OF WASHINGTON CONFERENCES HELD SINCE OCTOBER BETWEEN 
WILLIAM Se Be LACY, UeSe STATE DEPARTMENT OFFICIAL IN CHARGE OF 


EAST-WEST CULTURAL EXCHANGE, AND SOVIET AMBASSADOR GEORGI Ne 
ZAROUBIN. 


THE NEWSPAPER ADDED: 


AGREEMENTS SO FAR COVER SCIENTIFIC EXCHANGES IN A BROAD 
FIELD AND EXCHANGE OF INDUSTRIAL SPECIALISTS IN SUCH FIELDS AS 
METALLURGY, MINING, CHEMICALS, AND ELECTRIC POWER. 

THE CONFEREES ALSO HAVE APPROVED VISITS BETWEEN THE Two 
COUNTRIES OF EXPERTS ON CONSTRUCTION AND AGRICULTURE AND LEADERS OF 
VARIOUS FIELDS IN THE ARTS, EDUCATION AND ATHLETICS. 

STILL NOT AT THE AGREEMENT STAGE BUT PROGRESSING ARE TALKS 
ABOUT COMMERCIAL AIR TRAFFIC BETWEEN THE TWO NATIONS AND EXCHANGE oF 
INFORMATION ON PEACEFUL USES OF ATOMIC ENERGY. 

ON SOME QUESTIONS, HOWEVER, THE CONFERENCES HAVE FAILED TO PRODUCE 
EVEN AGREEMENT ®IN PRINCIPLE. 

THESE INCLUDE THE JAMMING OF UsS. BROADCASTS TO THE SOVIET 


PEOPLE, EXCHANGE OF RADIO AND TELEVISION BROADCASTS AND MOVIES 


AND 
“a. PLAN TO SEND A SUPERMARKET EXHIBIT TO THE MOSCOW FAIR NEXT 
@ 


THE TONE OF THE NEGOTIATIONS HAS BEEN DESCRIBED AS *FRIENDLY 
AND POSITIVE," WITH THE LACY-ZAROUBIN MEETINGS OCCURING MORE THAN 
ONCE A WEEK SINCE OCT. 28. 

THE TALKS ARE NOW IN RECESS PENDING ANNOUNCEMENT OF DETAILS OF 
THE AGREEMENTS, EXPECTED BEFORE ZAROUBIN LEAVES HIS POST THE 
MIDDLE OF NEXT MONTH.

TAIPEL. FORMOSA. DEC. 31 (AP)-CHTANG KAI-SHEK IN A NEW YEAR'S 
MESSAGE TO THE NATION TODAY SAID "THERE IS NO DOUBT THE FREE WORLD 
WOULD WIN SHOULD KHRUSHCHEV UNLEASH A GLOBAL WAR IN THE NEAR FUTURE.® 

CHIANG DEVOTED A LARCE PART OF HIS SPEECH TO DENUNCIATION OF 
KHRUSHCHEV, BRANDING HIM "HITLER AND STALIN ROLLED INTO ONE.” 

DECLARING THE "IRON CURTAIN IS CRACKING" CHIANG SAID 800 
MILLION PEOPLE IN EUROPE AND ASIA "ARE IN FERMENT AGAINST THEIR 
COMMUNIST DICTATORS." 

HE CONTENDED THIS WAS ESPECIALLY TRUE ON THE CHINESE MAINLAND 
WHERE HE ASSERTED NUMEROUS REVOLTS OCCURRED SINCE LAST SPRING. 

CHIANG REFERRED TO RUSSIAN LAUNCHINGS OF EARTH SATELLITES AND 
CLAIMS TO HAVE DEVELOPED INTERCONTINENTAL BALLISTIC MISSILES. 

HE SAID "THEY ATTEMPTED TO INTIMIDATE THE FREE WORLD AND SUPPRESS IN- 
TERNAL UNREST BY A SHOW OF TECHNOLOGICAL ACHIEVEMENT AND MILITARY 
MIGHT HOPING THEREBY TO AVERT IMPENDING COLLAPSE." 

"RUSSIA TODAY IS A COMBINATION OF THE STRENGTH OF HITLER'S 
GERMANY AND STALIN'S SOVIET EMPIRE PLUS THE GREAT POTENTIAL OF THE 
CHINESE MAINLAND. 

HE SAID IN KHRUSHCHEV'’S VIEW THIS IS THE MOMENT FOR RUSSIA TO 
START AN OFFENSIVE TO CONQUER THE WORLD. 

"IF HE SHOULD MISS THIS OPPORTUNITY, HE THINKS HE WOULD LOSE THE 
COMMUNIST WORLD REVOLUTION. THE CRISIS FACING THE WORLD TODAY 
THEREFORE IS MORE SERIOUS THAN AT ANY TIME SINCE WORLD WAR II.” 

BUT CHIANG SAID NEITHER THE INTERNATIONAL SITUATION NOR THE 
RELATIVE STRENGTH OF RUSSIA AND THE UNITED STATES HAD BEEN CHANGED 
SINCE THE RUSSIAN SPUTNIKS. 

®HOWEVER KHRUSHCHEV MAY BE BENT ON WAR, AN OBJECTIVE EXAMINATION 
OF RECENT EVENTS LEADS TO THE CONCLUSION.es. THAT RUSSIA STILL LACKS 
THE CAPABILITY AND COURAGE. TO START A WORLD WAR AT LEAST IN THE 
NEXT TWO AIDe 

HE SAID THIS WAS BECAUSE AS YET RUSSIA COULD NOT MASS-PRODUCE 
IcBMS NOR BUILD UP ENOUGH OF A STOCKPILE TO WIPE OUT HER ENEMIES IN 
ONE . 

"BUT NO MATTER WHAT RUSSIA WILL OR WILL NOT DO I BELIEVE 
1958 1S GOING BE A YEAR OF DECISION FOR THE FATE OF THE WORLD, 

CHIA :

(340) WEATHER CONTROL fa wd fj 

WASHINGTON. DEC. 31 CAP)-PRESIDENT HISENHOWER'S ADVISORY COMMITTEF 
ON WEATHER CONTROL REPORTED TO THE WHITE HOUSE TODAY. THEN WENT OUT OF 
EXISTENCE. THE REPORT CALLED FOR GREATER EFFORT TO LEARN HOW TO CON- 
TROL WEATHER AND CLIMATE--A FIELD WITH IMPORTANT DEFENSE IMPLICATIONS. 

THE COMMITTEE CONFINED ITS STUDY TO CIVILIAN ASPECTS OF WEATHER 
CONTROL--PRINCIPALLY CLOUD SEEDING--BUT ITS CHAIRMAN, HOWARD T. 
ORVILLE--EMPHASIZED AT A NEWS CONFERENCE THAT CONTROL OF THE WEATHER 
COULD BECOME A VITAL WEAPON IN THE COLD WAR WITH RUSSIA. 

ORVILLE, A RETIRED NAVY CAPTAIN, DID NOT SAY DIRECTLY THAT THIS 
COUNTRY SHOULD GET STARTED ON A VAST PROGRAM TO BEST THE SOVIETS IN 
EFFORTS TO HARNESS THE ELEMENTS. HOWEVER, HE QUOTED EMINENT SCIENTISTS 
WHO TOOK SUCH A VIEW. 

VANNEVAR BUSH, WARTIME HEAD OF THE OFFICE OF SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH, 
WAS QUOTED AS SAYING, *BY ALL MEANS LET US GET AT IT.® 

ORVILLE ALSO RECALLED RECENT SENATE TESTIMONY BY DR. EDWARD TELLER, 
"FATHER OF THE H-BOMB." THAT THE TIME MIGHT COME WHEN RUSSIA WOULD BE 
ABLE TO CONTROL WEATHER AND CLIMATE ON A VAST SCALE. 

THE ADVISORY COMMITTEE REPORTED TO EISENHOWER THAT SOUND KNOWLEDGE 
OF METEOROLOGICAL FORCES AND THEIR POSSIBLE CONTROL IS LACKING. THE 
GROUP CALLED FOR STEPPED UP RESEARCH IN THIS FIELD AND SAID SUCH EFFORTS 
SHOULD BE DIRECTED BY THE NATIONAL SCIENCE FOUNDATION. 

IN ITS STUDY OF CLOUD SEEDING WITH SILVER IODIDE, THE COMMITTEE 
SAID IT FOUND THAT SEEDING OF WINTER-TYPE STORM CLOUDS OVER THE 
WESTERN MOUNTAINS BROUGHT INCREASED PRECIPITATION IN THE RANGE OF 
10-15 PER CENTe IT SAID THE ODDS WERE VERY GREAT THAT THE INCREASE 
WAS THE RESULT OF SEEDING AND NOT NATURAL FORCES. | 

IN LEVEL SECTIONS, IT SAID, IT WAS NOT ABLE TO TURN UP EVIDENCE 
THAT PRECIPITATION COULD BE INCREASED AS GREATLY THROUGH SEEDING. BUT 
IT NOTED THAT RAINFALL IN SUCH AREAS VARIES GREATLY AND THAT IT WAS 
DIFFICULT TO PIN DOWN THE EFFECTS OF SEEDING. 

NO EVIDENCE WAS FOUND, IT REPORTED, THAT SEEDING EVER CAUSES 
A DECREASE IN PRECIPITATION. 

THE COMMITTEE WAS ESTABLISHED IN 1953 TO MAKE AN EVALUATION OF 
PUBLIC AND PRIVATE EXPERIMENTS IN WEATHER CONTROL. toad

CHICAGO, *BEGs31 (AP)-ADLAI E. STEVENSON TODAY ISSUED THE FOLLOWING 
STATEMENT WHICH HE SAID WAS IN RESPONSE TO A NUMBER OF REQUESTS: 

®THE NEW YEAR ARRIVES AT A PERILOUS TIME, WHEN AMERICA IS CONFRONTED 
WITH A FATEFUL PARADOX: THAT THERE IS A RACE OF ARMS IN WHICH WE MUST 
AGAIN DRAW ABREAST, BUT THAT THIS HAS NOW BECOME A RACE THAT NO 
ONE, NEITHER WE NOR ANY OTHER NATION, CAN EVER WIN. 

MY GREATEST CONCERN IS THAT THE DIVISION BETWEEN EAST AND WEST 
SO WE MUST EMPHASIZE OUR BASIC PEACEFUL PURPOSES 
AND IT IS WELL TO REMIND 
OURSELVES OF THE LESSON OF THE SATELLITES---THAT WE ARE PART F THE 
HUMAN FAMILY AND MUST LEARN TO LIVE NOT ONLY WITH OUR ALLIES BUT OUR 
ADVERSARIES." 

STEVENSON, FORMER GOVERNOR OF ILLINOIS AND NOW AN ATTORNEY IN 
CHICAGO, WAS THE DEMOCRATIC NOMINEE FOR PRESIDENT IN 1952 AND 1956.
